In this paper, we introduce ReWorld, a framework aimed to employ reinforcement learning to align the video generation with physical realism, task completion capability, embodiment plausibility and visual quality. Specifically, we first construct a large-scale (~235K) video preference dataset and employ it to train a hierarchical reward model designed to capture multi-dimensional reward consistent with human preferences. We further propose a practical alignment algorithm that post-trains flow-based video generators using this reward through a computationally efficient PPO-style algorithm. Comprehensive experiments and theoretical analysis demonstrate that ReWorld significantly improves the physical fidelity, logical coherence, embodiment and visual quality of generated rollouts, outperforming previous methods.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: MirrorComm: A Communication-Efficient Cooperative Perception Framework via Mirrored World Models
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Shenghan Luo, Yin Xu, Cixiao Zhang, Yang Wang, Yujie Cao
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: MirrorComm introduces a novel communication-efficient cooperative perception framework using mirrored world models to significantly reduce bandwidth requirements while preserving performance in object detection and segmentation tasks.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Cooperative perception (CP) requires substantial communication bandwidth to exchange sensing information among connected agents. A variety of compression techniques have been proposed to reduce transmission costs while retaining task-relevant information. However, most existing methods follow a frame-wise compression paradigm, overlooking temporal predictability and repeatedly transmitting information that could be inferred from historical context. To address these limitations, we propose MirrorComm, the first world model-based communication-efficient CP framework. Specifically, mirrored world models at the transmitter and receiver predict the transmitter's current observation from a shared history of its reconstructed observations. The transmitter compares this prediction with its current observation and selectively transmits observation updates to correct prediction errors, reducing repeated transmission of predictable information. Experiments on the OPV2V dataset across two downstream tasks including object detection and semantic segmentation show that MirrorComm reduces communication bandwidth requirements by up to approximately 66-fold while maintaining comparable performance to a state-of-the-art (SOTA) method. Ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of the individual components.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: UniGS-SLAM: Monocular Gaussian SLAM with Enhanced Geometry and Open-Vocabulary Semantics
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Xingyuan Ding, Sicheng Yu, Kaiyong Zhao, Hao Wang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: UniGS-SLAM is an RGB-only monocular SLAM framework that enhances geometric reconstruction and semantic mapping by decoupling semantics from Gaussian primitives, achieving superior performance and speed.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Monocular semantic SLAM aims to reconstruct scene geometry and build semantic maps from RGB observations. Existing Gaussian-based methods often attach semantic labels or features to evolving Gaussian primitives, making semantic fusion difficult to maintain and increasing reconstruction overhead. Hybrid Gaussian--voxel representations provide more stable semantic support, but often rely on RGB-D input or known poses and do not revise historical semantic evidence after geometry updates. We present UniGS-SLAM, an RGB-only framework that decouples open-vocabulary semantics from Gaussian reconstruction while preserving bidirectional interaction. Foundation priors enhance monocular depth and pose estimation, while semantic observations are fused into an independent sparse voxel map with observation provenance, enabling historical contributions to be revised as reconstruction evolves. The fused semantics further guide Gaussian filtering and local surface refinement. Experiments on Replica, ScanNet, and KITTI-360 show leading tracking, rendering, and geometric reconstruction performance among representative RGB-only methods, together with strong open-set semantic mapping on Replica and ScanNet. We also achieve a 2.37-fold reconstruction speedup over the fastest compared semantic SLAM baseline. Project page: https://3dagentworld.github.io/UniGS-SLAM/.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: LegoEnv: Self-Evolving Agentic Environments via Modular Recombination
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Zhuosong Jiang, Chengxu Wu, Junqi Liu, Yujie Yi, Siqin Wang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: LegoEnv introduces a modular approach to environment design, enabling the reuse and evolution of environment components, significantly improving agent performance across diverse applications.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: LLM agents learn by interacting with environments, yet existing environments are designed for specific tasks and fail to generalize to new ones. Recent methods automate environment construction with LLMs. However, they generate each environment from scratch, neither reusing parts shared across environments nor carrying a fix from one environment to the rest. To address this, we propose a new paradigm of evolving environment atoms, which composes environments from reusable atoms (intent, rule, data and server) and evolves the atoms when an environment fails to give reliable feedback (e.g., an application lacks a tool the task requires). To instantiate this paradigm, we introduce LegoEnv, which builds 5,465 verified environments over 223 applications, and one round of evolution raises the share of solvable environments from 71.6% to 88.3%. On AutomationBench, SFT on these environments lifts Qwen3.6-27B from 16.0% to 32.0%, and RL with their verifiers lifts Qwen3.8-27B from 37.6% to 40.3%. Further analyses show steady gains with corpus size, transfer to unseen applications, and failures concentrated in a few shared root causes.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: GazeVLA: Learning Human Intention for Robotic Manipulation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Chengyang Li, Kaiyi Xiong, Yuan Xu, Lei Qian, Yizhou Wang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: GazeVLA leverages human gaze to model intentions for robotic manipulation, enhancing learning from demonstrations and improving task execution across diverse embodiments.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Embodied foundation models have significantly propelled the advancement of artificial general intelligence, yet they rely heavily on large-scale data. Recent studies identify human behavior as one of the most scalable sources for fostering robotic physical intelligence. However, the inherent embodiment gap remains a fundamental challenge for effective human-to-robot learning. In this work, we model human intention to enable efficient learning from human demonstrations. Among human behavioral cues, gaze simultaneously encodes high-level task semantics and exhibits a synergistic coupling with low-level action. By modeling intention through gaze, we derive a mid-level representation that facilitates cross-embodiment knowledge transfer. We demonstrate that robots can internalize human intentions to enhance manipulation, even without robotic intention annotations. To capture the synergy between intention and action, we adopt a Chain-of-Thought reasoning paradigm during inference. Our approach enables the execution of long-horizon and fine-grained tasks across diverse embodiments. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms baseline approaches and generalizes to unseen settings. Project page: https://gazevla.github.io .

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: CompliantBot: Learning Whole-Body Compliance across Task Interfaces for Humanoid Control
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Haoyang Li, Keqi Zhu, Zhanxiang Cao, Yang Zhang, Yizhi Chen
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: CompliantBot is a novel compliance-training framework for humanoid robots that enables effective yielding to external forces while maintaining task performance without preconstructed data.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Humanoid controllers need the ability to yield to external forces while retaining the capacity to resume their original tasks. However, tracking objectives penalize the deviations needed for yielding, while relaxing tracking goals persistently can make task recovery harder. Existing approaches often rely on task-specific interaction command interfaces or constructed compliant motion data and reference trajectories, limiting the direct reuse of their compliance-training mechanisms across different task interfaces. We introduce CompliantBot, a compliance-training framework for motion tracking and velocity-command locomotion. It preserves the original task inputs and requires no preconstructed compliant data or target trajectories. A state-dependent interaction force field couples applied loads to the robot's motion, enabling local articulation and whole-body movement to change the forces experienced. A complementary force-magnitude reward encourages lower interaction loads, while task rewards are downweighted during loading and restored after release to coordinate yielding and task resumption. The trained policies use task inputs and proprioceptive history without explicit external-force measurements. Across both task interfaces, CompliantBot yields farther under constant pulls and experiences lower spring interaction loads than matched baselines, while resuming task tracking after force removal. CompliantBot achieves the highest task completion among the compared methods under stronger pulls. Power evaluations further show that CompliantBot has the lowest mean joint mechanical power among the compared methods. Real-robot demonstrations further illustrate compliant responses through arm motion, stepping, and body reorientation.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: RoboSnap: One-Shot Real-to-Sim Scene Generation for Generalizable Robot Learning and Evaluation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Shujie Zhang, Jingkun Yi, Weipeng Zhong, Zirui Zhou, Yangkun Zhu
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: RoboSnap enables efficient one-shot generation of simulation-ready scenes from real images, enhancing robot learning and evaluation through a layered design for stability and visual fidelity.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Recovering real-world scenes as interactive simulation environments can enable generalizable robot learning and reproducible policy evaluation. However, constructing scenes that are both physically stable and visually faithful remains slow and expensive. In this work, we present RoboSnap, a real-to-sim framework that turns a single RGB image into a simulation-ready scene. The key idea is a layered design that separates the physics-critical interaction area from the surrounding visual context: collision-aware foreground assets are refined for stable robot interaction, while a 3D Gaussian splatting visual layer preserves faithful background appearance under novel views. Experiments on DROID scenes and real-robot tasks show that RoboSnap achieves reliable trajectory replay in the recovered scenes, supports task-specific synthetic data generation for policy training, and yields meaningful sim-real correlation for policy evaluation. To further support real-to-sim research, we introduce DROID-Sim, a real-to-sim companion dataset constructed from 564 real-world scenes in DROID. Extensive experiments suggest that the value of real-to-sim methods lies not only in high-fidelity visual reconstruction, but in turning real environments into reusable infrastructure for robot learning and evaluation.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: PREM: Prediction-Regulated Memory for Robot Manipulation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Xiao Huang, Ya Zhang, Weidi Xie
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: PREM enhances robot manipulation by using action-conditioned future predictions to optimize memory learning and updating, significantly improving task success rates and robustness.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: A robot's next action can depend on recent motion or earlier visual evidence absent from its current observation. A recurrent visual-memory architecture can retain this history in a visual state, but its usefulness depends on what the state represents and how it is updated with new observations. We introduce Prediction-Regulated Memory (PREM), a framework that uses action-conditioned future prediction to guide both memory learning and updating in vision-language-action policies. During training, predicting future visual features provides temporal supervision for memory learning. During execution, PREM compares current visual features with the prediction made at the preceding decision and uses the spatially normalized prediction discrepancy to regulate updates to the visual state at each spatial location. The updated visual state supplies temporal context for action generation alongside current observations. Built on $π_{0.5}$, PREM improves average success rate from 9.63% to 20.74% on DOMINO dynamic manipulation tasks and from 14.4% to 83.8% on the RMBench M(1) memory-dependent setting. Further evaluations on LIBERO and LIBERO-Pro show improvements in general manipulation and robustness to spatial perturbations. PREM incurs a mean inference overhead of 7.7 ms on a single NVIDIA H800 GPU.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: TacMind: Benchmarking and Modeling Tactile Interaction States for Robotic Manipulation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Jiaxin Shi, Zibin Wu, Yichi Zhang, Jianghua Duan, Siyu Zhu
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: The paper introduces TacMind, a benchmark for evaluating tactile interaction in robotic manipulation, proposing a predictive model that enhances action generation through learned tactile states.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct observations of contact physics, local geometry, and interaction dynamics, making it a vital source of feedback for contact-rich manipulation. However, existing tactile manipulation studies are often developed and evaluated within specific task settings, making it difficult to systematically compare how tactile information contributes under different interaction conditions. In this work, we develop a benchmark in simulation comprising 128 tasks organized around three complementary evaluation regimes: Precise, Recognition, and Dynamic. The benchmark further includes controlled static and dynamic task variants and 12 perturbation settings for evaluating robustness under changes in visual and physical conditions. These settings motivate studying tactile information as a temporally evolving interaction representation rather than only as an instantaneous observation. We therefore propose an action-conditioned latent predictive world model that integrates tactile history and learns a tactile state through prediction of future tactile latents. Building on this representation, we design a model that conditions action generation on the learned tactile state and uses predicted future tactile information to refine candidate actions through predictive tactile reflection. Experiments on the proposed benchmark show consistent gains from incorporating tactile information across the evaluated regimes. Project Page: https://tacmind-bench.github.io/

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: SpecPrune-VLA: Accelerating Vision-Language-Action Models via Action-Aware Self-Speculative Pruning
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Hanzhen Wang, Jiaming Xu, Yushun Xiang, Jiayi Pan, Yongkang Zhou
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: SpecPrune-VLA enhances Vision-Language-Action model efficiency by integrating global context into a two-level pruning strategy, achieving significant speedups with minimal performance loss.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Pruning is a typical acceleration technique for compute-bound models by removing computation on unimportant values. Recently, it has been applied to accelerate Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model inference. However, existing acceleration methods focus on local information from the current action step and ignore the global context, leading to >20% success rate drop and limited speedup in some scenarios. In this paper, we point out spatial-temporal consistency in VLA tasks: input images in consecutive steps exhibit high similarity, and propose the key insight that token selection should combine local information with global context of the model. Based on this, we propose SpecPrune-VLA, a training-free, two-level pruning method with heuristic control. (1) Action-level static pruning. We leverage global history and local attention to statically reduce visual tokens per action. (2) Layer-level dynamic pruning. We prune tokens adaptively per layer based on layer-wise importance. (3) Lightweight action-aware controller: We classify actions as coarse- or fine-grained by the speed of the end effector and adjust pruning aggressiveness accordingly. Extensive experiments show that SpecPrune-VLA achieves up to 1.57$\times$ speedup in LIBERO simulation and 1.70$\times$ on real-world tasks, with negligible success rate degradation.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: GaussFlaw: Fine-Grained Perceptual Diagnosis for 3D Gaussian Splatting
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Shaocheng Shen, Zihan Zheng, Kejin Li, Lu Liu, Xiaoyun Zhang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: GaussFlaw introduces a large-scale dataset and a model, GeoCritic, for fine-grained diagnosis of rendering artifacts in 3D Gaussian Splatting, enhancing photorealistic synthesis.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic novel- view synthesis with real-time rendering, yet fine-grained di- agnosis of its rendering artifacts remains challenging. These artifacts are typically spatially localized and exhibit diverse degradation patterns, making them difficult to character- ize using global quality metrics and image-level assessment benchmarks, which provide no explicit indication of where they occur or what types of artifacts they represent. To ad- dress this limitation, we introduce GaussFlaw-80K, the first large-scale dataset for fine-grained perceptual diagnosis in 3DGS. Constructed through a model-assisted human-in-the- loop pipeline, GaussFlaw-80K contains 80,049 artifact re- gions across 14,289 rendered images, each annotated with a pixel-level mask and one of eight flaw labels spanning ge- ometric, blending, and photometric degradations. These an- notations turn 3DGS artifact diagnosis into an explicit and measurable task. Building on this dataset, we propose Ge- oCritic, a geometry-guided multi-task model that integrates RGB appearance with depth-derived cues to jointly localize artifacts and classify their flaw types. Beyond evaluation, we further demonstrate the downstream benefits of fine-grained diagnosis through three complementary targeted operations: Gaussian densification, attribute correction, and outlier prun- ing. Experiments show that GeoCritic achieves an AUC-J of 0.9507 and an Acc@1 of 80.08%, while diagnosis-guided re- finement improves all reported global and crop-level metrics across diverse datasets and 3DGS backbones.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: CoEnv: Code-Driven Exploration in Real-to-Sim Digital Twins for Multi-Arm Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Li Kang, Yutao Fan, Rui Li, Heng Zhou, Yiran Qin
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: CoEnv enables a coding agent to efficiently explore and refine multi-arm manipulation programs in a realistic digital twin, achieving higher success rates than previous methods.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: General-purpose coding agents can now write, debug, and refine entire robot programs, but only if they have somewhere to practice. Physical hardware is a poor practice ground: exploratory rollouts are slow to reset and, when several arms share a workspace, unsafe. Generic simulation benchmarks are safe but do not match the geometry, assets, or viewpoints of the workspace where the robot must actually work. We present CoEx (Code-driven Exploration), which lets the agent practice in an executable digital twin of its own deployment workspace. The twin is built by CoEnv, our real-to-sim framework, which reconstructs the physical scene from multi-view RGBD into a physics simulation. Inside it, a centralized code agent explores at the program level, writing a complete multi-arm program, running it in the twin, and refining it against grounded verification (privileged state checks, checkpoint predicates on risky steps, and adaptive viewpoints against inter-arm occlusion). Verified programs transfer to hardware through collision-checked deployment. On five real-world multi-arm tasks with up to three heterogeneous robots, CoEx reaches 70% average success, against 50% for the same system without the code agent (where a VLM must choose every primitive step by step), outperforms two prior VLM-planning frameworks, and produces verified episodes at 3.8-11.7x the ablated rate. Because every verified rollout is also a demonstration, exploration leaves reusable experience behind: a $π_{0.5}$ policy fine-tuned purely on 200 agent-generated rollouts reaches 100% and 70% real-robot success on two tasks, with no human demonstrations.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: NAS-PO: Native Attention-Strategy Policy Optimization for Vision-Language Models
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Ke An, Shizhe Xiang, Yue Liu, Liang Chen, Pei Fu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: NAS-PO introduces a novel reinforcement learning framework that optimizes vision-language models by leveraging native attention for enhanced perceptual relevance and improved reasoning performance.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective post-training paradigm for vision-language models (VLMs). Standard RLVR, however, assigns identical outcome-derived credit to all generated tokens regardless of their perceptual relevance. Recent perception-aware methods estimate visual reliance through image perturbation or masking. These indirect proxies require perturbation branches, while corruption sensitivity does not necessarily identify the visual evidence used for reasoning. We instead shape model perception through native attention, an intrinsic model signal. Rather than treating attention as a post-hoc explanation, we formulate it as a reward-anchored, token-aligned routing signal that encourages attention patterns supporting visually grounded reasoning. To this end, we propose NAS-PO, a Native Attention-Strategy Policy Optimization framework. NAS-PO analyzes native attention with a visual mass policy that quantifies visual allocation and a conditional visual policy that captures spatial routing over visual tokens, making the optimization well-posed. Based on this, Native Attention-Strategy Advantage Shaping (NAS-AS) draws on the visual-mass policy to redistribute signed policy-gradient credit for visually engaged rollouts. The Adaptive Attention-Coupled (AAC) loss then aligns the visual-mass policy on all response tokens and the conditional visual policy on visually active ones, consolidating the visual-routing patterns that drive successful trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that NAS-PO substantially surpasses leading RL-tuned VLMs across 7 out-of-domain reasoning and perception benchmarks, with its effectiveness consistently validated across 8B and 32B. Visual-Routing Sensitivity (VRS) analysis further indicates that the optimized attention prioritizes visually load-bearing regions.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: ArthroCut: Autonomous Policy Learning for Robotic Bone Resection in Knee Arthroplasty
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Xu Lu, Yiling Zhang, Wenquan Cheng, Longfei Ma, Fang Chen
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: ArthroCut enhances robotic knee arthroplasty by integrating multimodal data for autonomous, context-aware decision-making, achieving an 86% success rate in bone resection tasks.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Despite rapid commercialization of surgical robots, their autonomy and real-time decision-making remain limited in practice. To address this gap, we propose ArthroCut, an autonomous policy learning framework that upgrades knee arthroplasty robots from assistive execution to context-aware action generation. ArthroCut fine-tunes a Qwen--VL backbone on a self-built, time-synchronized multimodal dataset from 21 complete cases (23,205 RGB--D pairs), integrating preoperative CT/MR, intraoperative NDI tracking of bones and end effector, RGB--D surgical video, robot state, and textual intent. The method operates on two complementary token families -- Preoperative Imaging Tokens (PIT) to encode patient-specific anatomy and planned resection planes, and Time-Aligned Surgical Tokens (TAST) to fuse real-time visual, geometric, and kinematic evidence -- and emits an interpretable action grammar under grammar/safety-constrained decoding. In bench-top experiments on a knee prosthesis across seven trials, ArthroCut achieves an average success rate of 86% over the six standard resections, significantly outperforming strong baselines trained under the same protocol. Ablations show that TAST is the principal driver of reliability while PIT provides essential anatomical grounding, and their combination yields the most stable multi-plane execution. These results indicate that aligning preoperative geometry with time-aligned intraoperative perception and translating that alignment into tokenized, constrained actions is an effective path toward robust, interpretable autonomy in orthopedic robotic surgery.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: OmniPiano: Diverse Dexterous Piano-Playing Challenges for Standard, Robust, Safe, and Multi-Agent RL
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Fan Xu, Fan Yang, Yifan Xu, Ruiyuan Zhang, Yimou Wu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: OmniPiano introduces a modular benchmark for multi-agent RL in piano playing, enhancing evaluation with diverse tasks, safety constraints, and extensive algorithm comparisons.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Dexterous robotic manipulation remains a major challenge in robotics, exemplified by piano playing, which requires coordinated control of fingers and provides a demanding testbed for reinforcement learning (RL). Although previous work established a benchmark for robotic piano playing, it is restricted to two hands and does not support unified evaluation. To address this gap, we introduce OmniPiano, a benchmark that provides one to up to five Shadow Hands and supports standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent RL within a shared piano-playing task family. OmniPiano is developed for scalable and diverse piano-playing tasks with configurable perturbations, explicit safety constraints, and decentralized cooperation settings. Particularly, to facilitate usability and extendability, OmniPiano adopts a highly modular design and provides comprehensive tasks to support RL study of task performance, robustness, safety, and cooperation in dexterous control. With at least 912 task settings and 36 baseline algorithms, OmniPiano further incorporates LLM-based agents to broaden the evaluation scope and reveal new insights. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art RL algorithms and frontier LLM-based agents still struggle on challenging piano-playing tasks, even under standard RL settings, highlighting substantial room for improvement in dexterous control. The code, dataset, tutorial, and demo are available at https://sail-research-lab.github.io/omnipiano/.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yujiao Shen, Jiahe Song, Haitian Li, Jingkang Yang, Ziwei Liu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: EgoActionBench introduces a comprehensive benchmark for dense action captioning in egocentric videos, enhancing evaluation metrics and demonstrating significant improvements in model performance for fine-grained action understanding.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence, yet it requires models to accurately understand fine-grained human actions from egocentric observations. However, existing benchmarks remain limited in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association. We introduce EgoActionBench, a benchmark that represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. EgoActionBench contains 1,407 episodes with 41,132 human-refined action annotations. To evaluate such dense predictions, we propose an evaluation protocol that retrieves temporally eligible candidates, selects a prediction by content agreement, and scores semantic fidelity and temporal overlap alongside action precision and recall, jointly capturing what happens, when it happens, and which hand performs it. We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems on EgoActionBench and further adapt two backbones, Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning on automatically annotated training episodes. EgoAction improves EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points on the two backbones, and both adapted models outperform all open-source baselines. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations of current models in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association, highlighting the gap between general video understanding and the action understanding required for embodied intelligence.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: SelfImprove-Bench: Evaluating Generalization in Self-Improving Agents
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Bangrui Xu, Jie Yang, Sidi Chen, Xuanhe Zhou, Jiantao Qiu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: SelfImprove-Bench is a proposed evaluation framework for recursively self-improving agents, assessing their generalization across tasks in exploring, planning, and reasoning capabilities.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Recursively self-improving (RSI) systems are increasingly viewed as a promising means of accelerating progress toward artificial general intelligence. They aim to autonomously improve their capabilities by refining their working pipelines and recursively improving the strategies that guide subsequent refinements, with gains generalizing to unseen scenarios.However, existing evaluations lack reliable metrics to distinguish capability gains from scenario fitting, sustainable and extensible protocols for unseen tasks and difficulties, and fine-grained attribution of improvement to evolution traces. To this end, we propose SelfImprove-Bench,an RSI evaluation framework that organizes tasks into three primary capabilities (i.e., Exploring, Planning, Reasoning) as scenarios for guiding model evolution. We instantiated the tasks on games for controllability and reproducibility, and pairs them with scalable generation and orchestration driven by task templates and difficulty coefficients. Beyond task-level scores, SelfImprove-Bench organizes evaluation into generalization ladder levels G0 to G4 that measure how far gains transfer from training conditions. Experiments reveal that the evolutionary gains of existing RSI methods are inconsistent across generalization levels.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: What Drives the Zero-to-One Jump? Diagnosing and Steering Hard-Prompt Learning in RLVR
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Rui Zhu, Yumou Liu, Zhenzhe Zheng, Fan Wu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper explores the dynamics of zero-to-one transitions in RLVR, introducing NAPO to enhance early solution discovery by leveraging negative learning signals.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved mathematical reasoning, yet progress on hard prompts often stalls: a prompt can remain unsolved for many training steps before abruptly transitioning to solved--a discrete "zero-to-one" jump whose underlying dynamics and steerability remain poorly understood. We investigate two questions: what drives this transition, and can it be steered? Through event-based analysis measuring the time-to-first-positive (TTFP), we find that negative rollouts preceding successful transitions consistently retain higher early-stage generation entropy, distinguishing near-solvable failures from dead ends. This signal motivates NAPO (Negative-Augmented Policy Optimization), a method integrated with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) that ranks negatives in unsolved groups via an early-branching driver and assigns graded advantages, injecting informative gradients precisely where standard group-relative updates vanish. Under fixed rollout budgets, NAPO accelerates early solution discovery and improves Pass@256 by 10.0 points on AIME24 and 6.6 points on AIME2025, demonstrating that zero-to-one transitions are diagnosable and steerable through driver-guided negative learning. Our code is available at https://github.com/jameszhu-pixel-time/Z2O.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: CoSMO: Conformal Semantic Mapping for Open-World Safe Robot Navigation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Shuqi Wang, Yiwei Zheng, Pingrui Zhang, Yue Gao, Xiang Yin
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: CoSMO is a semantic safety mapping framework that enhances robot navigation by integrating conformal prediction with vision-language models for improved obstacle awareness and safety guarantees in dynamic environments.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Safe autonomous navigation requires not only geometric obstacle avoidance but also semantic awareness. Different object categories demand different safety clearances, and the set of relevant categories may expand as the robot explores novel environments. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer rich semantic representations for building maps of unknown scenes, yet their confidence scores are poorly calibrated, making raw predictions unreliable for safety-critical planning. Conformal prediction (CP) can provide coverage guarantees, but existing methods assume a fixed label set and stationary data, limiting their use in open-world settings. We propose Conformal Semantic Mapping for Open-World Safe Robot Navigation (CoSMO), a semantic safety mapping framework that transforms VLM embeddings into online-calibrated coverage sets and safety-aware obstacle dilations under distribution shift. By calibrating directly in the embedding space, CoSMO avoids the score rescaling that arises in confidence calibration as the vocabulary expands. Experiments on the Matterport3D (MP3D) dataset show that CoSMO reduces semantic collisions by 61.6% relative to a geometry-only baseline, while maintaining formal coverage guarantees even under delayed expert feedback. Real-world experiments on a quadruped robot further demonstrate generalization by achieving long-run empirical coverage of 90.73% against the 90% target. Project website: https://yangming911.github.io/cosmo-page/.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: ReWorld: Multi-Dimensional Reward Modeling for Embodied Video Generation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Baorui Peng, Wenyao Zhang, Liang Xu, Bohan Li, Hu Zhu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: ReWorld introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enhances embodied video generation by aligning it with physical realism, task logic, and visual quality through a multi-dimensional reward model.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Current embodied video generation models primarily emphasize visual generative quality while overlooking physical fidelity, dynamic consistency, and task logic, especially for contact-rich manipulation tasks, which limits their applicability to downstream tasks. In this paper, we introduce ReWorld, a framework aimed to employ reinforcement learning to align the video generation with physical realism, task completion capability, embodiment plausibility and visual quality. Specifically, we first construct a large-scale (~235K) video preference dataset and employ it to train a hierarchical reward model designed to capture multi-dimensional reward consistent with human preferences. We further propose a practical alignment algorithm that post-trains flow-based video generators using this reward through a computationally efficient PPO-style algorithm. Comprehensive experiments and theoretical analysis demonstrate that ReWorld significantly improves the physical fidelity, logical coherence, embodiment and visual quality of generated rollouts, outperforming previous methods.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: MirrorComm: A Communication-Efficient Cooperative Perception Framework via Mirrored World Models
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Shenghan Luo, Yin Xu, Cixiao Zhang, Yang Wang, Yujie Cao
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: MirrorComm introduces a novel communication-efficient cooperative perception framework using mirrored world models to significantly reduce bandwidth requirements while preserving performance in object detection and segmentation tasks.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Cooperative perception (CP) requires substantial communication bandwidth to exchange sensing information among connected agents. A variety of compression techniques have been proposed to reduce transmission costs while retaining task-relevant information. However, most existing methods follow a frame-wise compression paradigm, overlooking temporal predictability and repeatedly transmitting information that could be inferred from historical context. To address these limitations, we propose MirrorComm, the first world model-based communication-efficient CP framework. Specifically, mirrored world models at the transmitter and receiver predict the transmitter's current observation from a shared history of its reconstructed observations. The transmitter compares this prediction with its current observation and selectively transmits observation updates to correct prediction errors, reducing repeated transmission of predictable information. Experiments on the OPV2V dataset across two downstream tasks including object detection and semantic segmentation show that MirrorComm reduces communication bandwidth requirements by up to approximately 66-fold while maintaining comparable performance to a state-of-the-art (SOTA) method. Ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of the individual components.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: UniGS-SLAM: Monocular Gaussian SLAM with Enhanced Geometry and Open-Vocabulary Semantics
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Xingyuan Ding, Sicheng Yu, Kaiyong Zhao, Hao Wang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: UniGS-SLAM is an RGB-only monocular SLAM framework that enhances geometric reconstruction and semantic mapping by decoupling semantics from Gaussian primitives, achieving superior performance and speed.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Monocular semantic SLAM aims to reconstruct scene geometry and build semantic maps from RGB observations. Existing Gaussian-based methods often attach semantic labels or features to evolving Gaussian primitives, making semantic fusion difficult to maintain and increasing reconstruction overhead. Hybrid Gaussian--voxel representations provide more stable semantic support, but often rely on RGB-D input or known poses and do not revise historical semantic evidence after geometry updates. We present UniGS-SLAM, an RGB-only framework that decouples open-vocabulary semantics from Gaussian reconstruction while preserving bidirectional interaction. Foundation priors enhance monocular depth and pose estimation, while semantic observations are fused into an independent sparse voxel map with observation provenance, enabling historical contributions to be revised as reconstruction evolves. The fused semantics further guide Gaussian filtering and local surface refinement. Experiments on Replica, ScanNet, and KITTI-360 show leading tracking, rendering, and geometric reconstruction performance among representative RGB-only methods, together with strong open-set semantic mapping on Replica and ScanNet. We also achieve a 2.37-fold reconstruction speedup over the fastest compared semantic SLAM baseline. Project page: https://3dagentworld.github.io/UniGS-SLAM/.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: LegoEnv: Self-Evolving Agentic Environments via Modular Recombination
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Zhuosong Jiang, Chengxu Wu, Junqi Liu, Yujie Yi, Siqin Wang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: LegoEnv introduces a modular approach to environment design, enabling the reuse and evolution of environment components, significantly improving agent performance across diverse applications.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: LLM agents learn by interacting with environments, yet existing environments are designed for specific tasks and fail to generalize to new ones. Recent methods automate environment construction with LLMs. However, they generate each environment from scratch, neither reusing parts shared across environments nor carrying a fix from one environment to the rest. To address this, we propose a new paradigm of evolving environment atoms, which composes environments from reusable atoms (intent, rule, data and server) and evolves the atoms when an environment fails to give reliable feedback (e.g., an application lacks a tool the task requires). To instantiate this paradigm, we introduce LegoEnv, which builds 5,465 verified environments over 223 applications, and one round of evolution raises the share of solvable environments from 71.6% to 88.3%. On AutomationBench, SFT on these environments lifts Qwen3.6-27B from 16.0% to 32.0%, and RL with their verifiers lifts Qwen3.8-27B from 37.6% to 40.3%. Further analyses show steady gains with corpus size, transfer to unseen applications, and failures concentrated in a few shared root causes.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: GazeVLA: Learning Human Intention for Robotic Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Chengyang Li, Kaiyi Xiong, Yuan Xu, Lei Qian, Yizhou Wang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: GazeVLA leverages human gaze to model intentions for robotic manipulation, enhancing learning from demonstrations and improving task execution across diverse embodiments.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Embodied foundation models have significantly propelled the advancement of artificial general intelligence, yet they rely heavily on large-scale data. Recent studies identify human behavior as one of the most scalable sources for fostering robotic physical intelligence. However, the inherent embodiment gap remains a fundamental challenge for effective human-to-robot learning. In this work, we model human intention to enable efficient learning from human demonstrations. Among human behavioral cues, gaze simultaneously encodes high-level task semantics and exhibits a synergistic coupling with low-level action. By modeling intention through gaze, we derive a mid-level representation that facilitates cross-embodiment knowledge transfer. We demonstrate that robots can internalize human intentions to enhance manipulation, even without robotic intention annotations. To capture the synergy between intention and action, we adopt a Chain-of-Thought reasoning paradigm during inference. Our approach enables the execution of long-horizon and fine-grained tasks across diverse embodiments. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms baseline approaches and generalizes to unseen settings. Project page: https://gazevla.github.io .

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: CompliantBot: Learning Whole-Body Compliance across Task Interfaces for Humanoid Control
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Haoyang Li, Keqi Zhu, Zhanxiang Cao, Yang Zhang, Yizhi Chen
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: CompliantBot is a novel compliance-training framework for humanoid robots that enables effective yielding to external forces while maintaining task performance without preconstructed data.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Humanoid controllers need the ability to yield to external forces while retaining the capacity to resume their original tasks. However, tracking objectives penalize the deviations needed for yielding, while relaxing tracking goals persistently can make task recovery harder. Existing approaches often rely on task-specific interaction command interfaces or constructed compliant motion data and reference trajectories, limiting the direct reuse of their compliance-training mechanisms across different task interfaces. We introduce CompliantBot, a compliance-training framework for motion tracking and velocity-command locomotion. It preserves the original task inputs and requires no preconstructed compliant data or target trajectories. A state-dependent interaction force field couples applied loads to the robot's motion, enabling local articulation and whole-body movement to change the forces experienced. A complementary force-magnitude reward encourages lower interaction loads, while task rewards are downweighted during loading and restored after release to coordinate yielding and task resumption. The trained policies use task inputs and proprioceptive history without explicit external-force measurements. Across both task interfaces, CompliantBot yields farther under constant pulls and experiences lower spring interaction loads than matched baselines, while resuming task tracking after force removal. CompliantBot achieves the highest task completion among the compared methods under stronger pulls. Power evaluations further show that CompliantBot has the lowest mean joint mechanical power among the compared methods. Real-robot demonstrations further illustrate compliant responses through arm motion, stepping, and body reorientation.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: RoboSnap: One-Shot Real-to-Sim Scene Generation for Generalizable Robot Learning and Evaluation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Shujie Zhang, Jingkun Yi, Weipeng Zhong, Zirui Zhou, Yangkun Zhu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: RoboSnap enables efficient one-shot generation of simulation-ready scenes from real images, enhancing robot learning and evaluation through a layered design for stability and visual fidelity.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Recovering real-world scenes as interactive simulation environments can enable generalizable robot learning and reproducible policy evaluation. However, constructing scenes that are both physically stable and visually faithful remains slow and expensive. In this work, we present RoboSnap, a real-to-sim framework that turns a single RGB image into a simulation-ready scene. The key idea is a layered design that separates the physics-critical interaction area from the surrounding visual context: collision-aware foreground assets are refined for stable robot interaction, while a 3D Gaussian splatting visual layer preserves faithful background appearance under novel views. Experiments on DROID scenes and real-robot tasks show that RoboSnap achieves reliable trajectory replay in the recovered scenes, supports task-specific synthetic data generation for policy training, and yields meaningful sim-real correlation for policy evaluation. To further support real-to-sim research, we introduce DROID-Sim, a real-to-sim companion dataset constructed from 564 real-world scenes in DROID. Extensive experiments suggest that the value of real-to-sim methods lies not only in high-fidelity visual reconstruction, but in turning real environments into reusable infrastructure for robot learning and evaluation.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: PREM: Prediction-Regulated Memory for Robot Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Xiao Huang, Ya Zhang, Weidi Xie
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: PREM enhances robot manipulation by using action-conditioned future predictions to optimize memory learning and updating, significantly improving task success rates and robustness.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: A robot's next action can depend on recent motion or earlier visual evidence absent from its current observation. A recurrent visual-memory architecture can retain this history in a visual state, but its usefulness depends on what the state represents and how it is updated with new observations. We introduce Prediction-Regulated Memory (PREM), a framework that uses action-conditioned future prediction to guide both memory learning and updating in vision-language-action policies. During training, predicting future visual features provides temporal supervision for memory learning. During execution, PREM compares current visual features with the prediction made at the preceding decision and uses the spatially normalized prediction discrepancy to regulate updates to the visual state at each spatial location. The updated visual state supplies temporal context for action generation alongside current observations. Built on $π_{0.5}$, PREM improves average success rate from 9.63% to 20.74% on DOMINO dynamic manipulation tasks and from 14.4% to 83.8% on the RMBench M(1) memory-dependent setting. Further evaluations on LIBERO and LIBERO-Pro show improvements in general manipulation and robustness to spatial perturbations. PREM incurs a mean inference overhead of 7.7 ms on a single NVIDIA H800 GPU.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: TacMind: Benchmarking and Modeling Tactile Interaction States for Robotic Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Jiaxin Shi, Zibin Wu, Yichi Zhang, Jianghua Duan, Siyu Zhu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper introduces TacMind, a benchmark for evaluating tactile interaction in robotic manipulation, proposing a predictive model that enhances action generation through learned tactile states.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct observations of contact physics, local geometry, and interaction dynamics, making it a vital source of feedback for contact-rich manipulation. However, existing tactile manipulation studies are often developed and evaluated within specific task settings, making it difficult to systematically compare how tactile information contributes under different interaction conditions. In this work, we develop a benchmark in simulation comprising 128 tasks organized around three complementary evaluation regimes: Precise, Recognition, and Dynamic. The benchmark further includes controlled static and dynamic task variants and 12 perturbation settings for evaluating robustness under changes in visual and physical conditions. These settings motivate studying tactile information as a temporally evolving interaction representation rather than only as an instantaneous observation. We therefore propose an action-conditioned latent predictive world model that integrates tactile history and learns a tactile state through prediction of future tactile latents. Building on this representation, we design a model that conditions action generation on the learned tactile state and uses predicted future tactile information to refine candidate actions through predictive tactile reflection. Experiments on the proposed benchmark show consistent gains from incorporating tactile information across the evaluated regimes. Project Page: https://tacmind-bench.github.io/

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: SpecPrune-VLA: Accelerating Vision-Language-Action Models via Action-Aware Self-Speculative Pruning
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Hanzhen Wang, Jiaming Xu, Yushun Xiang, Jiayi Pan, Yongkang Zhou
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: SpecPrune-VLA enhances Vision-Language-Action model efficiency by integrating global context into a two-level pruning strategy, achieving significant speedups with minimal performance loss.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Pruning is a typical acceleration technique for compute-bound models by removing computation on unimportant values. Recently, it has been applied to accelerate Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model inference. However, existing acceleration methods focus on local information from the current action step and ignore the global context, leading to >20% success rate drop and limited speedup in some scenarios. In this paper, we point out spatial-temporal consistency in VLA tasks: input images in consecutive steps exhibit high similarity, and propose the key insight that token selection should combine local information with global context of the model. Based on this, we propose SpecPrune-VLA, a training-free, two-level pruning method with heuristic control. (1) Action-level static pruning. We leverage global history and local attention to statically reduce visual tokens per action. (2) Layer-level dynamic pruning. We prune tokens adaptively per layer based on layer-wise importance. (3) Lightweight action-aware controller: We classify actions as coarse- or fine-grained by the speed of the end effector and adjust pruning aggressiveness accordingly. Extensive experiments show that SpecPrune-VLA achieves up to 1.57$\times$ speedup in LIBERO simulation and 1.70$\times$ on real-world tasks, with negligible success rate degradation.

南方科技大学.title: Aerial Content-Aware Sample-Adaptive Classifier for Urban Photogrammetric Point Cloud Segmentation
南方科技大学.authors_text: Chong Liu, Yonghua Lu, Zhanglin Cheng
南方科技大学.summary: The Aerial Content-Aware Sample-Adaptive Classifier (ACASAC) enhances urban photogrammetric point cloud segmentation by integrating decision-level adaptation with feature fusion, improving classification accuracy significantly.
南方科技大学.debug_abstract: Urban photogrammetric point clouds are commonly processed as local 3D patches, limiting the context available for distinguishing geometrically similar categories. Orthographic projection of the same data yields a co-registered digital orthophoto map (DOM)/RGB-D representation that supports efficient large-context modeling but compresses vertical geometry. Existing projection--point methods mainly fuse these two representations at the feature level while retaining a classifier shared across all samples. We present the Aerial Content-Aware Sample-Adaptive Classifier (ACASAC), which complements feature fusion with decision-level adaptation. A point-aligned aerial region bridges the full aerial crop and local 3D patch. ACASAC models scene-to-local variation within the projection and the representation discrepancy between aligned 2D and 3D supports, then transfers both relations to refine the local point class representation. The refined representation, scene-level aerial context, and fixed fused-head prior jointly form a classifier for the current sample. ACASAC improves the fixed dual-representation head by 2.1 and 2.7 mIoU points on SensatUrban and UrbanBIS, respectively, and by 2.1--2.3 points across four tested encoder combinations.

南方科技大学.title: Dual-Grained Policy Optimization for Hallucination Reduction in Flow-Based RL
南方科技大学.authors_text: Xiaofeng Tan, Jun Liu, Yuanting Fan, Bin-Bin Gao, Xi Jiang
南方科技大学.summary: This paper presents Dual-Grained Policy Optimization (DGPO) to reduce visual hallucinations in flow-based reinforcement learning by balancing global semantics and local details through dynamic noise scheduling.
南方科技大学.debug_abstract: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) on flow-based models is crucial for alignment. However, they often introduce visual hallucinations like over-optimized details and semantic misalignment. This work explains why visual hallucinations arise and shows how to reduce them. We first investigate RFT methods from a unified perspective and trace hallucinations to two mechanisms. Limited exploration from stochastic differential equation (SDE) rollouts yields detail-dominated within-group differences, leading to fine-grained optimization that over-emphasizes local details and neglects global semantics. Trajectory imitation writes reward-selected SDE noise into the velocity field, leading to inconsistent optimization that degrades cross-step consistency. Building on this, we propose DGPO, a general framework to mitigate hallucinations. Specifically, we design Dynamic Granularity Rollout (DGR) to balance global semantics and local details by dynamically scheduling noise sources. We then introduce a Consistent Policy Gradient Optimization that preserves the consistency by aligning the policy with a more stable prior. Experiments show that DGPO reduces low-/high-level hallucinations by 49%/38% and improves the average of out-of-domain (OoD) metrics by +4.9% on FLUX.1.dev, compared with the baseline's -0.7%. Project page: https://xiaofeng-tan.github.io/projects/ConsistentRFT/

天津大学.title: DiffCap-Bench: A Comprehensive, Challenging, Robust Benchmark for Image Difference Captioning
天津大学.authors_text: Yuancheng Wei, Haojie Zhang, Linli Yao, Lei Li, Jiali Chen
天津大学.summary: DiffCap-Bench introduces a robust benchmark for Image Difference Captioning, addressing existing evaluation gaps and enhancing multimodal language model assessments through diverse categories and human-validated metrics.
天津大学.debug_abstract: Image Difference Captioning (IDC) generates natural language descriptions that precisely identify differences between two images, serving as a key benchmark for fine-grained change perception, cross-modal reasoning, and image editing data construction. However, existing benchmarks lack diversity and compositional complexity, and standard lexical-overlap metrics (e.g., BLEU, METEOR) fail to capture semantic consistency or penalize hallucinations, which together prevent a comprehensive and robust evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on IDC. To address these gaps, we introduce DiffCap-Bench, a comprehensive IDC benchmark covering ten distinct difference categories to ensure diversity and compositional complexity. Furthermore, we propose an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation protocol grounded in human-validated Difference Lists, enabling a robust assessment of models' ability to both capture and describe visual changes. Through extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art MLLMs, we reveal significant performance gaps between proprietary and open-source models, highlight the critical importance of reasoning capability, and identify clear limitations in model scaling. Our framework also demonstrates strong alignment with human expert judgments and strong correlation with downstream image editing data construction quality. These findings establish DiffCap-Bench as both a reliable IDC evaluation framework and a practical predictor of downstream utility. The benchmark and code will be made publicly available to support further research.

天津大学.title: NAS-PO: Native Attention-Strategy Policy Optimization for Vision-Language Models
天津大学.authors_text: Ke An, Shizhe Xiang, Yue Liu, Liang Chen, Pei Fu
天津大学.summary: NAS-PO introduces a novel reinforcement learning framework that optimizes vision-language models by leveraging native attention for enhanced perceptual relevance and improved reasoning performance.
天津大学.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective post-training paradigm for vision-language models (VLMs). Standard RLVR, however, assigns identical outcome-derived credit to all generated tokens regardless of their perceptual relevance. Recent perception-aware methods estimate visual reliance through image perturbation or masking. These indirect proxies require perturbation branches, while corruption sensitivity does not necessarily identify the visual evidence used for reasoning. We instead shape model perception through native attention, an intrinsic model signal. Rather than treating attention as a post-hoc explanation, we formulate it as a reward-anchored, token-aligned routing signal that encourages attention patterns supporting visually grounded reasoning. To this end, we propose NAS-PO, a Native Attention-Strategy Policy Optimization framework. NAS-PO analyzes native attention with a visual mass policy that quantifies visual allocation and a conditional visual policy that captures spatial routing over visual tokens, making the optimization well-posed. Based on this, Native Attention-Strategy Advantage Shaping (NAS-AS) draws on the visual-mass policy to redistribute signed policy-gradient credit for visually engaged rollouts. The Adaptive Attention-Coupled (AAC) loss then aligns the visual-mass policy on all response tokens and the conditional visual policy on visually active ones, consolidating the visual-routing patterns that drive successful trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that NAS-PO substantially surpasses leading RL-tuned VLMs across 7 out-of-domain reasoning and perception benchmarks, with its effectiveness consistently validated across 8B and 32B. Visual-Routing Sensitivity (VRS) analysis further indicates that the optimized attention prioritizes visually load-bearing regions.

天津大学.title: Safety4DM: A Vision-Language Framework for Risk-Aware Dynamic Maps in Vehicle-Road-Cloud Collaborative Driving
天津大学.authors_text: Zhengshu Zhou, Shaoyu Wang, Lu Tao, Xinhui Hu, Jiaqi Gu
天津大学.summary: Safety4DM introduces a vision-language framework enhancing dynamic maps for vehicle-road-cloud driving by integrating risk-aware data and a natural language interface for improved safety.
天津大学.debug_abstract: Dynamic map (DM) is a core information infrastructure for vehicle-road-cloud (VRC) cooperative autonomous driving. It fuses perception data from multiple sources to overcome the inherent line-of-sight and field-of-view limits of single-vehicle perception. However, DM still falls short on driving safety in two ways. First, DM data specifications already define road conditions semantically, but no pipeline yet turns real-world road observations into fine-grained risk entities in the DM. Second, existing DM systems lack a natural language interface for driving risks. To close these gaps, we propose Safety4DM, a safety-oriented language system for VRC dynamic maps. We first build RoadRisk, a real-world road image dataset that covers four types of road conditions and four risk levels. On this dataset, we fine-tune a vision-language model (VLM) for road safety risk perception. The model outputs structured risk representations that the DM can ingest directly. We then introduce a Safety-aware Step-wise Prompting (SafeStep) mechanism as the natural language query interface of the DM. SafeStep answers queries accurately and also generates actionable driving advice. To build and evaluate this interface, we develop SafeVRC-Sim, a VRC cooperative simulation framework, and SafeDM-QA, a safety question-answering benchmark. Experiments show that even the compact Qwen3-VL-4B reaches 89.83% accuracy on risk perception after fine-tuning. SafeStep also plugs easily into multiple LLM families. With medium and large models (20B and above) from five families, it achieves over 93% natural language query accuracy in every case, which shows strong generalization.

天津大学.title: Knowledge-Guided Floodwater Level Reasoning for Cloud-Edge Collaborative Monitoring
天津大学.authors_text: Zhengshu Zhou, Shaoyu Wang, Ziyi Geng, Lu Tao, Qian Long
天津大学.summary: The HydroReasoner framework enhances floodwater level detection through explicit visual reasoning and cloud-edge collaboration, improving accuracy and efficiency while reducing computational load.
天津大学.debug_abstract: Frequent urban floodwater poses a serious threat to the safety and efficiency of intelligent transportation systems. Existing vision-based methods for floodwater level detection face two main limitations. First, the lack of explicit reasoning leads to poor detection performance and little interpretability. Second, these methods struggle to generalize to the complex and varied real-world road scenes seen from different viewpoints. To address this, we reformulate the task as an explicit visual reasoning problem and propose HydroReasoner, a floodwater level reasoning framework designed for cloud-edge collaboration. HydroReasoner builds on Qwen2.5-VL and is trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization. To address the scarcity of reasoning process annotations, we build a floodwater domain knowledge graph HydroKG and design a novel KG path reward. Through deterministic graph traversal over HydroKG, this reward supervises the model's reasoning process at a fine granularity, which improves both reasoning and generalization. For edge deployment, we apply 4-bit quantization to the model, cutting GPU memory usage by 57% and inference latency by 43% while out-of-domain accuracy drops by only 0.2 percentage points. We also propose a confidence-based cloud-edge routing mechanism, which improves system safety and eases the computational load on the cloud. In addition, we build HydroLevel, a floodwater benchmark dataset of 3,000 images, for training and evaluating the model. Experimental results show that HydroReasoner achieves detection accuracy 4.0 and 13.6 percentage points higher than conventional vision baselines in the in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations respectively, with performance dropping by only 4.4 percentage points out of domain.

天津大学.title: AgenticMobility: An Open-Source Platform for Multi-AI-Agent Mobility Dynamics
天津大学.authors_text: Jiaheng Xiao, Jiangtao Han, Jiachen Wang, Honghai Li, Lijun Sun
天津大学.summary: AgenticMobility is an open-source platform enabling the study of multi-AI-agent interactions in urban mobility dynamics, facilitating experiments on adaptation and policy impacts.
天津大学.debug_abstract: Understanding mobility dynamics and the effects of urban transportation management policies requires examining how individual travel decisions, traffic conditions, and policy interventions influence one another over time. We present AgenticMobility, an open-source experimental platform for studying how mobility AI agents and other AI agents interact, adapt through repeated experience, and collectively shape mobility outcomes. Persistent agents retain identities and relevant states across rounds, with explicit interfaces defining information access, admissible actions, and decision schedules; linked records trace decisions, execution, and feedback. In the current implementation, large language model (LLM) agents act as travelers choosing routes and departure times and as a manager periodically adjusting link charges within MATSim. A preliminary demonstration spans 100 simulated days in each of five configurations, with one run per configuration and a shared simulation seed. In the joint traveler--manager run, all 1,179,300 finalized target decisions satisfied action constraints; execution checks verified implementation of accepted choices and preservation of personal memories across days. Trajectories show stable route choices alongside departure-time adjustments and differences between controlled-trip and population-wide outcomes. The platform supports experiments on individual adaptation, collective outcomes, and management interventions by varying information access, retained experience, and management feedback. Source code is available at https://github.com/Agentic-City-Research/Agentic-Mobility

天津大学.title: ReinSeg: Retrieval-Guided Bounded Multimodal Refinement for 3-D Road Anomaly Segmentation
天津大学.authors_text: Haifa Zhang, Yijing Wang, Zhiqiang Zuo
天津大学.summary: ReinSeg enhances 3-D road anomaly segmentation by integrating LiDAR and imagery for improved hazard detection, achieving significant performance gains on the STU benchmark.
天津大学.debug_abstract: 3-D road anomaly segmentation is essential for risk-aware perception in autonomous driving. Its central challenge is to rank sparsely observed hazards ahead of abundant normal road structures while preserving point-wise metric localization. LiDAR provides accurate 3-D point support, whereas surround-view imagery offers complementary semantic context for separating unexpected hazards from challenging normal structures. We propose ReinSeg, a retrieval-guided bounded multimodal refinement framework for point-wise road anomaly segmentation. Occupied LiDAR bird's-eye-view cells retrieve scene-specific context from a shared memory of eight surround-view images without supplying calibration variables to the retrieval module. A relative-norm-bounded residual returns this context to the LiDAR point features, so the frozen LIDO anomaly-scoring interface is preserved, and the refinement is optimized with in-distribution semantic labels only. On the Spotting the Unexpected (STU) benchmark, ReinSeg improves validation average precision from 27.54\% to 35.67\% and reduces the false-positive rate at 95\% anomaly recall from 34.85\% to 10.61\%, shrinking the high-recall screening set from 67.54 to 20.55 million points. Relative to REL, AP is 24.99 percentage points higher and FPR95 is 0.99 points lower. Matched interfaces and component isolation show that retrieved scene imagery and the relative-norm bound are both essential, and ReinSeg stays above LiDAR-only performance under missing, corrupted, or misaligned camera inputs while running at 21.8 frames per second. These results establish bounded retrieval of scene-specific visual evidence as an effective route to reliable 3-D road-hazard perception.

天津大学.title: IMPose: Closed-Loop Correction Propagation for Interactive Multi-Person Pose Annotation
天津大学.authors_text: Haoyang Ge, Jian Ma, Ziwen Wang, Qihe Wang, Jianqi Fan
天津大学.summary: IMPose introduces a correction-conditioned framework for interactive multi-person pose annotation, enhancing accuracy through refined temporal inference and closed-loop correction propagation.
天津大学.debug_abstract: High-quality dynamic human pose annotations provide important supervision for learning fine-grained human motion, yet dense multi-person video annotation remains labor-intensive. Sparse human corrections can reduce this effort, but their propagated locations may become unreliable and ambiguous across identities. Existing interactive refinement and temporal propagation methods do not explicitly address how imperfect propagated corrections should participate in subsequent multi-person pose inference. We propose IMPose, a correction-conditioned temporal inference framework for interactive multi-person pose annotation. IMPose separates temporal correspondence from pose estimation: propagated corrections are treated as geometric priors rather than final predictions and are refined by a correction-aware decoder using target-frame visual evidence. A keypoint-aware identity state further combines structured pose geometry with trajectory history to preserve person- and joint-level correspondence. The refined pose and identity state are fed back to subsequent frames, forming a closed temporal correction loop. Under a controlled sparse-correction protocol on PoseTrack21, one correction improves mean average precision (mAP) from 38.87 to 67.99 and Higher Order Tracking Accuracy (HOTA) from 52.21 to 64.89. At a 20-frame correction interval, IMPose achieves 89.03% keypoint-level Object Keypoint Similarity (K-OKS), compared with 81.41% for CoTracker and 70.12% for PoseWarper-based propagation. We further extend PoseTrack21 with 188K additional person instances through 3.55M annotation updates to keypoints, bounding boxes, and person IDs using 100 annotator-hours. The annotation tool, code, and extended dataset will be released.

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).title: Learning to Build: Autonomous Robotic Assembly of Stable Structures Without Predefined Plans
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Jingwen Wang, Johannes Kirschner, Paul Rolland, Luis Salamanca, Stefana Parascho
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).summary: This paper introduces a reinforcement learning framework enabling autonomous robots to construct stable structures adaptively, without predefined plans, using targets and obstacles.
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: This paper presents a novel autonomous robotic assembly framework for constructing stable structures without relying on predefined architectural blueprints. Instead of following fixed plans, construction tasks are defined through targets and obstacles, allowing the system to adapt more flexibly to environmental uncertainty and variations during the building process. A reinforcement learning (RL) policy, trained using deep Q-learning with successor features, serves as the decision-making component. As a proof of concept, we evaluate the approach on a benchmark of 15 2D robotic assembly tasks of discrete block construction. Experiments using a real-world closed-loop robotic setup demonstrate the feasibility of the method and its ability to handle construction noise. The results suggest that our framework offers a promising direction for more adaptable and robust robotic construction in real-world environments.

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Jiaheng Xiao, Jiangtao Han, Jiachen Wang, Honghai Li, Lijun Sun

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: Understanding mobility dynamics and the effects of urban transportation management policies requires examining how individual travel decisions, traffic conditions, and policy interventions influence one another over time.
