深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Lookahead Prediction-Guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing for Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Mengzhao Wang, Yanli Ji, Peng Ye
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The paper presents LPAVR, a framework that enhances multimodal reasoning by dynamically refocusing visual evidence based on anticipated reasoning needs, addressing Temporal Evidence Myopia.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning improves the visual reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models by dynamically incorporating visual evidence during reasoning. However, existing methods primarily select evidence from historical context. When the reasoning focus shifts, history-guided evidence may remain focused on prior regions and fail to cover the visual information required by the next step. We refer to this lag between visual evidence and subsequent reasoning demands as Temporal Evidence Myopia. To address this issue, we propose Lookahead Prediction-guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing (LPAVR), a training-free test-time framework. LPAVR transforms Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) from a decoding acceleration mechanism into a lookahead signal for anticipating upcoming reasoning intent. During MTP decoding, the draft head generates multiple future tokens, while the target model verifies them in parallel and retains the longest prefix consistent with its decoding trajectory. This target-verified prefix contains near-future semantics, which LPAVR uses to construct lookahead-guided visual evidence and assess whether history-guided evidence covers the indicated regions. If the coverage is sufficient, the history-guided evidence is retained; otherwise, LPAVR switches to the lookahead-guided evidence. This better aligns the visual context with upcoming reasoning and improves consistency between draft predictions and target-model decoding. Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that LPAVR improves both reasoning accuracy and the acceptance rates of MTP speculative tokens, jointly enhancing visual reasoning and speculative decoding efficiency.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Reconstruction as Spatial Evaluation: Diagnosing Cross-View Spatial Intelligence in Large Vision-Language Models
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Junfei Wu, Qiuyue Wang, Xuhong Huang, Qihang Peng, Mingsheng Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The paper introduces RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models' spatial intelligence through multi-view 3D scene reconstruction, revealing significant gaps in structural and metric accuracy.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: The spatial intelligence of large vision-language models (LVLMs) requires the ability to combine local visual observations into a geometrically consistent representation of the physical world. Many static benchmarks assess isolated spatial judgments, such as relative direction or distance, while interactive embodied evaluations combine perception with exploration, planning, control, and simulator-specific execution. To bridge this gap, we introduce RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark centered on multi-view 3D scene reconstruction across indoor, tabletop, and outdoor environments. Given real multi-view images and target-object queries, LVLMs are required to jointly predict oriented 3D bounding boxes in a shared, camera-anchored metric coordinate frame. Reconstructions are evaluated along two complementary axes: Structure for relative layout and Metric for physical scale and camera-anchored placement. Nine atomic spatial QA tasks, grouped into Geometric Perception and Spatial Relations, probe spatial capabilities involved in joint reconstruction. Offline navigation extends evaluation to path planning. Evaluation of 18 frontier LVLMs reveals a consistent gap between relative scene structure and metric reconstruction; even GPT-6-Astra scores 81.4% on Structure but only 58.7% on Metric. Tracing this gap, diagnostic analyses link atomic spatial capabilities to reconstruction quality and show that relational consistency alone does not ensure metric accuracy. Experiments with 3D map injection further separate scene construction from path planning, revealing how these geometric errors limit navigation success. Finally, spatial fine-tuning yields broad transfer across both spatial and general vision-language benchmarks.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: OmniPiano: Diverse Dexterous Piano-Playing Challenges for Standard, Robust, Safe, and Multi-Agent RL
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Fan Xu, Fan Yang, Yifan Xu, Ruiyuan Zhang, Yimou Wu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: OmniPiano introduces a modular benchmark for multi-agent RL in piano playing, enhancing evaluation with diverse tasks, safety constraints, and extensive algorithm comparisons.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Dexterous robotic manipulation remains a major challenge in robotics, exemplified by piano playing, which requires coordinated control of fingers and provides a demanding testbed for reinforcement learning (RL). Although previous work established a benchmark for robotic piano playing, it is restricted to two hands and does not support unified evaluation. To address this gap, we introduce OmniPiano, a benchmark that provides one to up to five Shadow Hands and supports standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent RL within a shared piano-playing task family. OmniPiano is developed for scalable and diverse piano-playing tasks with configurable perturbations, explicit safety constraints, and decentralized cooperation settings. Particularly, to facilitate usability and extendability, OmniPiano adopts a highly modular design and provides comprehensive tasks to support RL study of task performance, robustness, safety, and cooperation in dexterous control. With at least 912 task settings and 36 baseline algorithms, OmniPiano further incorporates LLM-based agents to broaden the evaluation scope and reveal new insights. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art RL algorithms and frontier LLM-based agents still struggle on challenging piano-playing tasks, even under standard RL settings, highlighting substantial room for improvement in dexterous control. The code, dataset, tutorial, and demo are available at https://sail-research-lab.github.io/omnipiano/.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Zhicheng He, Xiaohan Xing, Hongqiu Wang, Kun Yuan, Guankun Wang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: SurgPace introduces a complexity-aware framework for progressive distillation of surgical multimodal large language models, enhancing efficiency and stability in training through tailored supervision strategies.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Positive Safety Margins from Artificial Potential Field Reward Augmentation for Size-Robust Obstacle Avoidance under Partial Observability
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The paper demonstrates that augmenting reinforcement learning rewards with an artificial potential field can significantly enhance obstacle avoidance safety margins under partial observability, achieving high success rates.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Collision-free reaching is central to manipulation, yet real cells often leave the size and exact position of an obstacle unobserved, which excludes reinforcement learning controllers that take obstacle geometry as input. A reward limited to a collision penalty does not depend on the clearance outside the obstacle, so under a step cost its learned policy skims the obstacle surface and fails once the obstacle radius exceeds its training value. We investigate whether a single analytic reward term can induce a safety margin without exposing the obstacle to the policy. We augment the reward of a simulated Franka Emika Panda reaching task with a horizontal artificial potential field that penalizes proximity within a safety margin around each of two pillars (fixed nominal layout, random drift). Under hidden observation, policies trained with this term maintain a safe success rate above 88% across a radius sweep from 0.03 m to 0.055 m (30 seeds), while policies without it fall below 10% at the maximum tested radius; the term induces a minimum clearance of 47.9 mm against 9.6 mm without it and eliminates training collisions at least eight times earlier (median steps). The advantage is statistically significant at all out-of-distribution radii and holds across three reinforcement learning solvers and under full observation. Its safe success rate is comparable to that of a classical potential-field planner given the pillar positions. The margin is a fixed buffer rather than an adaptation to the radius, and it lengthens the path by about 19%.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: PointPilot: Unified Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric 3D Point Flow Prediction
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yihan Fang, Yuxin Tian, Ruixiang Wang, Zhanqi Zhang, Xing Hu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: PointPilot is a unified robotic manipulation framework that predicts 3D point flow for task-focused objects, enabling zero-shot generalization across diverse embodiments and manipulation modes.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Generalization remains a central challenge in robotics, calling for policies that address domain variations from multiple dimensions such as diverse embodiments, camera poses, and/or scene layouts. In order to approach this problem, we introduce PointPilot, a task-focused and 3D aligned manipulation framework built on a 3D space point-flow prediction. Rather than modeling the global scene, PointPilot only represents task-focused objects (robot grippers treated as objects), avoiding the prediction of potentially redundant scene parts unrelated to the manipulation tasks. Moreover, PointPilot aligns 3D spatial representation in one unified coordinate and supports closed-loop and fully automatic action execution across different manipulation modes from object point flow without a separately trained action expert, while existing works typically need an extra action head or are (semi-)automatic and single-arm mode specific. Given sensor observations and language instructions, our model jointly learns subtask planning, task-relevant object grounding, and 3D point flow prediction in an end-to-end way. By processing heterogeneous data in a shared 3D point flow space, PointPilot is able to absorb demonstrations from different embodiments. Extensive simulative and real world experiments validate our method. Notably, we demonstrate zero-shot embodiment generalization with PointPilot. A single trained policy can be deployed on previously unseen embodiments and successfully complete manipulation tasks without any additional fine-tuning.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Efficient Agentic Audio-Visual Question Answering through Toolset Pruning and Modality Consolidation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Peter Bell
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: This paper demonstrates that a compact omni-modal agent for audio-visual question answering can achieve similar or improved accuracy while reducing inference costs by 70% compared to specialized agents.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Fine-grained audio-visual question answering (AVQA) requires models to resolve complex cross-modal correspondences and temporally grounding from sparsely distributed evidence. Omni-modal agents, which autonomously orchestrate perception tools to actively collect evidence, achieve strong performance, but it remains unclear whether active perception from both audio and visual modalities depends on broad specialized toolsets, especially audio or visual modality-specific tools. Such systems may also introduce long execution trajectories and substantial inference cost. We investigate whether comparable performance can be retained with a compact workflow exposing only essential perceptual capabilities. Starting from the specialized-tool OmniAgent, we conduct staged controlled experiments that prune the toolset and progressively consolidate modality-specific tools into omni-modal tools, motivating a two-tool agent comprising only Omni-modal captioning and Omni-modal QA. Across three widely used AVQA benchmarks, our compact agent achieves comparable or better accuracy than the specialized-tool agent while reducing inference cost by around 70%.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: UA-Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Restoration for Material-Agnostic Object Manipulation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Rui Cao, Jia-Hui Pan, Yin Zhang, Qiwei Meng, Jiapeng Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: UA-Depth is an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that enhances robotic manipulation by improving depth accuracy for non-Lambertian objects through iterative co-refinement and uncertainty-gated features.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation requires accurate metric depth, yet commodity RGB-D cameras often fail on non-Lambertian objects such as transparent, reflective, and translucent materials, producing holes, structured noise, and biased depth. Most restoration methods produce only a single depth map, treating noisy and reliable regions uniformly for downstream tasks while ignoring regional uncertainty. We present UA-Depth, an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that iteratively co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty, and uses uncertainty-gated features to suppress unreliable cues for stable updates. To strengthen zero-shot behavior, UA-Depth leverages a frozen depth foundation model as a prior to initialize missing or unreliable depth, and applies two-stage MAD-weighted log-depth scale normalization to reduce outlier bias in relative-to-metric alignment. We introduce an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark across diverse scenes, materials, and sensors. Across these benchmarks, UA-Depth achieves the best mean rank among representative baselines, with particularly strong gains on datasets dominated by transparent and reflective objects. Beyond depth metrics, we demonstrate downstream improvements in category-level 6D pose estimation and 6D grasp synthesis by exploiting the predicted uncertainty. \emph{Code, models, and data for training and evaluation will be released upon publication.}

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: ExeWorldBench: Benchmarking Code-Based Executable 3D World Modeling
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Xinge Peng, Zhen Fang, Ruibing Wang, Yongxuan Lv, Haodong Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: ExeWorldBench is a novel benchmark for evaluating code-based 3D world modeling, integrating world understanding and executable realization across three progressively challenging tasks.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Coding agents are increasingly evolving beyond reproducing what a world looks like toward constructing executable worlds that capture how a world works. This shift calls for executable world modeling, which integrates two core capabilities: world understanding, reasoning about the underlying structural, mechanical, and causal principles of a world, and executable realization, translating that understanding into a code-based system whose behavior emerges from physical interactions. However, existing benchmarks provide only fragmented evaluations centered on physical reasoning, visual fidelity, or behavioral correctness, leaving the integration of these capabilities insufficiently assessed. To bridge this gap, we introduce ExeWorldBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark to comprehensively evaluate world understanding and executable realization through code-based 3D world construction. ExeWorldBench comprises three progressively challenging tasks: Mechanism Executability, which evaluates the realization of individual mechanisms from visual observations; Compositional Executability, which extends to multi-stage systems with spatial, mechanical, and causal dependencies; and Intent-Driven Executable World Synthesis, which requires constructing executable worlds from high-level goals and physical requirements. Extensive experiments on frontier models reveal substantial limitations in executable world modeling, offering insights into the development of more physically grounded and causally coherent world construction systems.

潘佳老师实验室.title: PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Ruikai Li, Naiyu Gao, Hao Shan, Yizhe Fan, Yanhao Wu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: PlanContext introduces a benchmark for evaluating context-aware driving decision-making, revealing that high trajectory quality does not guarantee effective in-context decisions across various driving scenarios.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Real-world driving requires context-aware decision-making. Existing end-to-end driving benchmarks primarily assess trajectory quality through safety, compliance, comfort, and driving progress, leaving context-dependent decision-making insufficiently characterized. To fill this gap, we present PlanContext, a benchmark for evaluating in-context driving decision-making. PlanContext constructs paired evaluations by varying high-level driving intentions while keeping the observed scene fixed, enabling a natural and controllable assessment of context-dependent decision-making. We further define six representative driving contexts and jointly evaluate contextual decision correctness, road compliance, and dynamic safety with class-balanced metrics. Experiments on 9,561 scene-condition instances from NAVSIM and 23 public end-to-end driving models show that high conventional driving-quality scores do not consistently correspond to strong route-level in-context driving decision-making. Further analysis shows that model behavior varies with decision timing, road structure, and traffic interaction depending on the decision required by the current context. Our results highlight in-context driving decision-making as an important complementary dimension for evaluating end-to-end driving systems.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Lookahead Prediction-Guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing for Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Mengzhao Wang, Yanli Ji, Peng Ye
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper presents LPAVR, a framework that enhances multimodal reasoning by dynamically refocusing visual evidence based on anticipated reasoning needs, addressing Temporal Evidence Myopia.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning improves the visual reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models by dynamically incorporating visual evidence during reasoning. However, existing methods primarily select evidence from historical context. When the reasoning focus shifts, history-guided evidence may remain focused on prior regions and fail to cover the visual information required by the next step. We refer to this lag between visual evidence and subsequent reasoning demands as Temporal Evidence Myopia. To address this issue, we propose Lookahead Prediction-guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing (LPAVR), a training-free test-time framework. LPAVR transforms Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) from a decoding acceleration mechanism into a lookahead signal for anticipating upcoming reasoning intent. During MTP decoding, the draft head generates multiple future tokens, while the target model verifies them in parallel and retains the longest prefix consistent with its decoding trajectory. This target-verified prefix contains near-future semantics, which LPAVR uses to construct lookahead-guided visual evidence and assess whether history-guided evidence covers the indicated regions. If the coverage is sufficient, the history-guided evidence is retained; otherwise, LPAVR switches to the lookahead-guided evidence. This better aligns the visual context with upcoming reasoning and improves consistency between draft predictions and target-model decoding. Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that LPAVR improves both reasoning accuracy and the acceptance rates of MTP speculative tokens, jointly enhancing visual reasoning and speculative decoding efficiency.

潘佳老师实验室.title: DiffCap-Bench: A Comprehensive, Challenging, Robust Benchmark for Image Difference Captioning
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yuancheng Wei, Haojie Zhang, Linli Yao, Lei Li, Jiali Chen
潘佳老师实验室.summary: DiffCap-Bench introduces a robust benchmark for Image Difference Captioning, addressing existing evaluation gaps and enhancing multimodal language model assessments through diverse categories and human-validated metrics.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Image Difference Captioning (IDC) generates natural language descriptions that precisely identify differences between two images, serving as a key benchmark for fine-grained change perception, cross-modal reasoning, and image editing data construction. However, existing benchmarks lack diversity and compositional complexity, and standard lexical-overlap metrics (e.g., BLEU, METEOR) fail to capture semantic consistency or penalize hallucinations, which together prevent a comprehensive and robust evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on IDC. To address these gaps, we introduce DiffCap-Bench, a comprehensive IDC benchmark covering ten distinct difference categories to ensure diversity and compositional complexity. Furthermore, we propose an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation protocol grounded in human-validated Difference Lists, enabling a robust assessment of models' ability to both capture and describe visual changes. Through extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art MLLMs, we reveal significant performance gaps between proprietary and open-source models, highlight the critical importance of reasoning capability, and identify clear limitations in model scaling. Our framework also demonstrates strong alignment with human expert judgments and strong correlation with downstream image editing data construction quality. These findings establish DiffCap-Bench as both a reliable IDC evaluation framework and a practical predictor of downstream utility. The benchmark and code will be made publicly available to support further research.

潘佳老师实验室.title: The Alignment Illusion: How BadReward Corrupts Text-to-Image Generation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Kaiwen Duan, Hongwei Yao, Yufei Chen, Ziyun Li, Tong Qiao
潘佳老师实验室.summary: This paper introduces BadReward, a novel attack exploiting Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback vulnerabilities in text-to-image models, demonstrating effective reward signal corruption through clean-label poisoning.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Modern text-to-image generative models increasingly rely on Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to align generated content with human preferences and safety standards. This post-training stage is critical for optimizing models toward high-fidelity and value-aligned behaviors using human preference data. However, while previous works have extensively investigated poisoning attacks against the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) stage of text-to-image training, the security vulnerabilities introduced by the RLHF process remain unexplored. In this paper, we present the first exploration into the feasibility of poisoning the RLHF process as a novel attack surface for compromising text-to-image models. We introduce BadReward, an indirect clean-label poisoning attack that manipulates reward signals to embed malicious behaviors. Our approach leverages a feature collision mechanism to produce poison preference image pairs that are visually benign, but aligned with a malicious target concept in the reward feature space. Our experiments demonstrate that this manipulation effectively corrupts the reward signal. Online RLHF further amplifies this corruption through its reward-model feedback loop, whereas offline preference optimization learns directly from the poisoned preferences. Finally, we demonstrate the real-world effectiveness of BadReward on modern text-to-image architectures, showing high attack success rates and visual stealthiness across different RLHF algorithms. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZJUICSR/BadReward.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Reconstruction as Spatial Evaluation: Diagnosing Cross-View Spatial Intelligence in Large Vision-Language Models
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Junfei Wu, Qiuyue Wang, Xuhong Huang, Qihang Peng, Mingsheng Li
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models' spatial intelligence through multi-view 3D scene reconstruction, revealing significant gaps in structural and metric accuracy.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: The spatial intelligence of large vision-language models (LVLMs) requires the ability to combine local visual observations into a geometrically consistent representation of the physical world. Many static benchmarks assess isolated spatial judgments, such as relative direction or distance, while interactive embodied evaluations combine perception with exploration, planning, control, and simulator-specific execution. To bridge this gap, we introduce RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark centered on multi-view 3D scene reconstruction across indoor, tabletop, and outdoor environments. Given real multi-view images and target-object queries, LVLMs are required to jointly predict oriented 3D bounding boxes in a shared, camera-anchored metric coordinate frame. Reconstructions are evaluated along two complementary axes: Structure for relative layout and Metric for physical scale and camera-anchored placement. Nine atomic spatial QA tasks, grouped into Geometric Perception and Spatial Relations, probe spatial capabilities involved in joint reconstruction. Offline navigation extends evaluation to path planning. Evaluation of 18 frontier LVLMs reveals a consistent gap between relative scene structure and metric reconstruction; even GPT-6-Astra scores 81.4% on Structure but only 58.7% on Metric. Tracing this gap, diagnostic analyses link atomic spatial capabilities to reconstruction quality and show that relational consistency alone does not ensure metric accuracy. Experiments with 3D map injection further separate scene construction from path planning, revealing how these geometric errors limit navigation success. Finally, spatial fine-tuning yields broad transfer across both spatial and general vision-language benchmarks.

潘佳老师实验室.title: OmniPiano: Diverse Dexterous Piano-Playing Challenges for Standard, Robust, Safe, and Multi-Agent RL
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Fan Xu, Fan Yang, Yifan Xu, Ruiyuan Zhang, Yimou Wu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: OmniPiano introduces a modular benchmark for multi-agent RL in piano playing, enhancing evaluation with diverse tasks, safety constraints, and extensive algorithm comparisons.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Dexterous robotic manipulation remains a major challenge in robotics, exemplified by piano playing, which requires coordinated control of fingers and provides a demanding testbed for reinforcement learning (RL). Although previous work established a benchmark for robotic piano playing, it is restricted to two hands and does not support unified evaluation. To address this gap, we introduce OmniPiano, a benchmark that provides one to up to five Shadow Hands and supports standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent RL within a shared piano-playing task family. OmniPiano is developed for scalable and diverse piano-playing tasks with configurable perturbations, explicit safety constraints, and decentralized cooperation settings. Particularly, to facilitate usability and extendability, OmniPiano adopts a highly modular design and provides comprehensive tasks to support RL study of task performance, robustness, safety, and cooperation in dexterous control. With at least 912 task settings and 36 baseline algorithms, OmniPiano further incorporates LLM-based agents to broaden the evaluation scope and reveal new insights. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art RL algorithms and frontier LLM-based agents still struggle on challenging piano-playing tasks, even under standard RL settings, highlighting substantial room for improvement in dexterous control. The code, dataset, tutorial, and demo are available at https://sail-research-lab.github.io/omnipiano/.

潘佳老师实验室.title: DiffGIPC: Differentiable Mixed-Coordinate Contact Mechanics on GPU
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Kemeng Huang, Bowen Ren, Xinyu Lu, Minchen Li, Taku komura
潘佳老师实验室.summary: DiffGIPC is a GPU-accelerated framework that optimizes contact-rich inverse problems in robotics, achieving significant speedups while ensuring non-penetration in simulations of deformable and rigid bodies.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Contact-rich inverse problems require efficient gradients and reliable enforcement of non-penetration. Existing differentiable methods provide fast simulation and rigid-deformable coupling, but contact treatments based on penalties or velocity-level constraints can permit penetration or positional drift. Incremental Potential Contact (IPC) maintains non-penetration through geometric barriers and {continuous collision detection (CCD)}. However, repeated forward and backward evaluations remain costly in full-space finite-element (FEM) implementations, particularly when nearly rigid components retain many vertex {degrees of freedom (DoFs)}. We present DiffGIPC, a GPU-accelerated differentiable IPC framework for optimizing interacting deformable and nearly rigid bodies. Our affine-body derivatives enable {rest-shape} design, initial-state optimization, and articulated control while retaining only twelve motion DoFs per affine body. These gradients account for how changes in geometry, placement, and actuation affect other objects through collision and friction. We preserve these interactions in one coupled FEM-affine adjoint system per frame, reducing the backward-system size without discarding the dependencies that drive the inverse problem. GPU-optimized backward computation further reduces the cost of repeated gradient evaluations. A reusable PyTorch interface connects supported physical parameters to user-defined parameter maps and losses across design, identification, motion, placement, and articulated control. Experiments demonstrate peak speedups over DiffIPC of approximately 150.0x with full-space FEM and 4133.3x with affine bodies for combined forward simulation and backward differentiation.

潘佳老师实验室.title: ROOF: Learning Humanoid Fall Recovery under Overhead Constraints
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yidan Lu, Jiayuan Yu, Zongrui Cai, Jingwen Sun, Jinrui Han
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper presents a reinforcement learning approach for humanoid fall recovery under overhead constraints, achieving significant success in both simulation and real-world scenarios.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: A fallen humanoid beneath an overhead obstacle faces a coupled recovery problem. It must create clearance while organizing support for a stable rise, since attempting to stand before making room can further increase obstruction. We introduce a reinforcement learning method with contact-supported geometric escape guidance, which rewards incremental reduction of robot-obstacle overlap without prescribing an escape path. To achieve this, a learned motion prior, together with posture-dependent support and joint-stall costs, is proposed to shape a single policy that learns when to clear the obstacle, how to establish support, and when to complete the rise, all using proprioception alone. In simulation, it recovers in 88.5% of trials beneath plates that can only be lifted, compared with 18.9% without geometric guidance, and in 98.6% of trials beneath free plates with randomized size, mass and placement. On a Unitree G1, the deployed policy recovered in 95 of 150 attempts across seven real-world obstacle scenes, including furniture and multi-object arrangements absent from training. Project page: https://lu-yidan.github.io/ROOF/

潘佳老师实验室.title: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Zhicheng He, Xiaohan Xing, Hongqiu Wang, Kun Yuan, Guankun Wang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: SurgPace introduces a complexity-aware framework for progressive distillation of surgical multimodal large language models, enhancing efficiency and stability in training through tailored supervision strategies.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Positive Safety Margins from Artificial Potential Field Reward Augmentation for Size-Robust Obstacle Avoidance under Partial Observability
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper demonstrates that augmenting reinforcement learning rewards with an artificial potential field can significantly enhance obstacle avoidance safety margins under partial observability, achieving high success rates.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Collision-free reaching is central to manipulation, yet real cells often leave the size and exact position of an obstacle unobserved, which excludes reinforcement learning controllers that take obstacle geometry as input. A reward limited to a collision penalty does not depend on the clearance outside the obstacle, so under a step cost its learned policy skims the obstacle surface and fails once the obstacle radius exceeds its training value. We investigate whether a single analytic reward term can induce a safety margin without exposing the obstacle to the policy. We augment the reward of a simulated Franka Emika Panda reaching task with a horizontal artificial potential field that penalizes proximity within a safety margin around each of two pillars (fixed nominal layout, random drift). Under hidden observation, policies trained with this term maintain a safe success rate above 88% across a radius sweep from 0.03 m to 0.055 m (30 seeds), while policies without it fall below 10% at the maximum tested radius; the term induces a minimum clearance of 47.9 mm against 9.6 mm without it and eliminates training collisions at least eight times earlier (median steps). The advantage is statistically significant at all out-of-distribution radii and holds across three reinforcement learning solvers and under full observation. Its safe success rate is comparable to that of a classical potential-field planner given the pillar positions. The margin is a fixed buffer rather than an adaptation to the radius, and it lengthens the path by about 19%.

潘佳老师实验室.title: PointPilot: Unified Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric 3D Point Flow Prediction
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yihan Fang, Yuxin Tian, Ruixiang Wang, Zhanqi Zhang, Xing Hu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: PointPilot is a unified robotic manipulation framework that predicts 3D point flow for task-focused objects, enabling zero-shot generalization across diverse embodiments and manipulation modes.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Generalization remains a central challenge in robotics, calling for policies that address domain variations from multiple dimensions such as diverse embodiments, camera poses, and/or scene layouts. In order to approach this problem, we introduce PointPilot, a task-focused and 3D aligned manipulation framework built on a 3D space point-flow prediction. Rather than modeling the global scene, PointPilot only represents task-focused objects (robot grippers treated as objects), avoiding the prediction of potentially redundant scene parts unrelated to the manipulation tasks. Moreover, PointPilot aligns 3D spatial representation in one unified coordinate and supports closed-loop and fully automatic action execution across different manipulation modes from object point flow without a separately trained action expert, while existing works typically need an extra action head or are (semi-)automatic and single-arm mode specific. Given sensor observations and language instructions, our model jointly learns subtask planning, task-relevant object grounding, and 3D point flow prediction in an end-to-end way. By processing heterogeneous data in a shared 3D point flow space, PointPilot is able to absorb demonstrations from different embodiments. Extensive simulative and real world experiments validate our method. Notably, we demonstrate zero-shot embodiment generalization with PointPilot. A single trained policy can be deployed on previously unseen embodiments and successfully complete manipulation tasks without any additional fine-tuning.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Self-Evolving Agentic Workflows via Semantic Decomposition of Complex Tasks
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Zichuan Fu, Junjia Qi, Xian Wu, Wenlin Zhang, Yimin Deng
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper presents a framework for self-evolving agentic workflows that optimizes complex task execution through semantic decomposition and iterative refinement based on execution feedback.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Agentic workflows organize complex tasks into reusable procedures. However, invoking an LLM at every step incurs repeated inference costs and delays. We propose a framework for self-evolving agentic workflows through semantic task decomposition. Each subtask has explicit applicability conditions and a procedure that executes code or invokes a model as needed. An agent uses execution feedback to refine the decomposition and update these procedures. Experiments in the GLEE competition show the framework on bargaining, negotiation and persuasion. Most observed final-decision procedures are implemented in code. Code is available at https://github.com/Applied-Machine-Learning-Lab/NeurIPS2026_SeaFlow.

潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Sicheng Yu, Liu Liu, Xinjie Wang, Xinjiang Wang, Taojun Ding
潘佳老师实验室.summary: GSExplorer introduces a persistent 3D Gaussian world state for interactive world generation, enhancing scene consistency and camera control through a novel generation-reconstruction framework.

Generated videos are then fed back to a SLAM-based reconstruction backend, where inconsistency filtering prevents conflicting content from corrupting the scene and cross-chunk bundle adjustment improves spatial alignment across generation steps. GSExplorer achieves the best overall performance among the compared methods on both single-step and three-step WorldScore evaluation, with strong camera control and consistency across both settings, including a Camera Control score of 99.07 in single-step extrapolation. 潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Xinge Peng, Zhen Fang, Ruibing Wang, Yongxuan Lv, Haodong Li
潘佳老师实验室.summary: ExeWorldBench is a novel benchmark for evaluating code-based 3D world modeling, integrating world understanding and executable realization across three progressively challenging tasks.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Coding agents are increasingly evolving beyond reproducing what a world looks like toward constructing executable worlds that capture how a world works. This shift calls for executable world modeling, which integrates two core capabilities: world understanding, reasoning about the underlying structural, mechanical, and causal principles of a world, and executable realization, translating that understanding into a code-based system whose behavior emerges from physical interactions. However, existing benchmarks provide only fragmented evaluations centered on physical reasoning, visual fidelity, or behavioral correctness, leaving the integration of these capabilities insufficiently assessed. To bridge this gap, we introduce ExeWorldBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark to comprehensively evaluate world understanding and executable realization through code-based 3D world construction. ExeWorldBench comprises three progressively challenging tasks: Mechanism Executability, which evaluates the realization of individual mechanisms from visual observations; Compositional Executability, which extends to multi-stage systems with spatial, mechanical, and causal dependencies; and Intent-Driven Executable World Synthesis, which requires constructing executable worlds from high-level goals and physical requirements. Extensive experiments on frontier models reveal substantial limitations in executable world modeling, offering insights into the development of more physically grounded and causally coherent world construction systems.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Lookahead Prediction-Guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing for Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Mengzhao Wang, Yanli Ji, Peng Ye
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The paper presents LPAVR, a framework that enhances multimodal reasoning by dynamically refocusing visual evidence based on anticipated reasoning needs, addressing Temporal Evidence Myopia.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning improves the visual reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models by dynamically incorporating visual evidence during reasoning. However, existing methods primarily select evidence from historical context. When the reasoning focus shifts, history-guided evidence may remain focused on prior regions and fail to cover the visual information required by the next step. We refer to this lag between visual evidence and subsequent reasoning demands as Temporal Evidence Myopia. To address this issue, we propose Lookahead Prediction-guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing (LPAVR), a training-free test-time framework. LPAVR transforms Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) from a decoding acceleration mechanism into a lookahead signal for anticipating upcoming reasoning intent. During MTP decoding, the draft head generates multiple future tokens, while the target model verifies them in parallel and retains the longest prefix consistent with its decoding trajectory. This target-verified prefix contains near-future semantics, which LPAVR uses to construct lookahead-guided visual evidence and assess whether history-guided evidence covers the indicated regions. If the coverage is sufficient, the history-guided evidence is retained; otherwise, LPAVR switches to the lookahead-guided evidence. This better aligns the visual context with upcoming reasoning and improves consistency between draft predictions and target-model decoding. Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that LPAVR improves both reasoning accuracy and the acceptance rates of MTP speculative tokens, jointly enhancing visual reasoning and speculative decoding efficiency.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: The Alignment Illusion: How BadReward Corrupts Text-to-Image Generation
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Kaiwen Duan, Hongwei Yao, Yufei Chen, Ziyun Li, Tong Qiao
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: This paper introduces BadReward, a novel attack exploiting Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback vulnerabilities in text-to-image models, demonstrating effective reward signal corruption through clean-label poisoning.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Modern text-to-image generative models increasingly rely on Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to align generated content with human preferences and safety standards. This post-training stage is critical for optimizing models toward high-fidelity and value-aligned behaviors using human preference data. However, while previous works have extensively investigated poisoning attacks against the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) stage of text-to-image training, the security vulnerabilities introduced by the RLHF process remain unexplored. In this paper, we present the first exploration into the feasibility of poisoning the RLHF process as a novel attack surface for compromising text-to-image models. We introduce BadReward, an indirect clean-label poisoning attack that manipulates reward signals to embed malicious behaviors. Our approach leverages a feature collision mechanism to produce poison preference image pairs that are visually benign, but aligned with a malicious target concept in the reward feature space. Our experiments demonstrate that this manipulation effectively corrupts the reward signal. Online RLHF further amplifies this corruption through its reward-model feedback loop, whereas offline preference optimization learns directly from the poisoned preferences. Finally, we demonstrate the real-world effectiveness of BadReward on modern text-to-image architectures, showing high attack success rates and visual stealthiness across different RLHF algorithms. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZJUICSR/BadReward.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Reconstruction as Spatial Evaluation: Diagnosing Cross-View Spatial Intelligence in Large Vision-Language Models
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Junfei Wu, Qiuyue Wang, Xuhong Huang, Qihang Peng, Mingsheng Li
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The paper introduces RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models' spatial intelligence through multi-view 3D scene reconstruction, revealing significant gaps in structural and metric accuracy.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: The spatial intelligence of large vision-language models (LVLMs) requires the ability to combine local visual observations into a geometrically consistent representation of the physical world. Many static benchmarks assess isolated spatial judgments, such as relative direction or distance, while interactive embodied evaluations combine perception with exploration, planning, control, and simulator-specific execution. To bridge this gap, we introduce RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark centered on multi-view 3D scene reconstruction across indoor, tabletop, and outdoor environments. Given real multi-view images and target-object queries, LVLMs are required to jointly predict oriented 3D bounding boxes in a shared, camera-anchored metric coordinate frame. Reconstructions are evaluated along two complementary axes: Structure for relative layout and Metric for physical scale and camera-anchored placement. Nine atomic spatial QA tasks, grouped into Geometric Perception and Spatial Relations, probe spatial capabilities involved in joint reconstruction. Offline navigation extends evaluation to path planning. Evaluation of 18 frontier LVLMs reveals a consistent gap between relative scene structure and metric reconstruction; even GPT-6-Astra scores 81.4% on Structure but only 58.7% on Metric. Tracing this gap, diagnostic analyses link atomic spatial capabilities to reconstruction quality and show that relational consistency alone does not ensure metric accuracy. Experiments with 3D map injection further separate scene construction from path planning, revealing how these geometric errors limit navigation success. Finally, spatial fine-tuning yields broad transfer across both spatial and general vision-language benchmarks.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: OmniPiano: Diverse Dexterous Piano-Playing Challenges for Standard, Robust, Safe, and Multi-Agent RL
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Fan Xu, Fan Yang, Yifan Xu, Ruiyuan Zhang, Yimou Wu
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: OmniPiano introduces a modular benchmark for multi-agent RL in piano playing, enhancing evaluation with diverse tasks, safety constraints, and extensive algorithm comparisons.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Dexterous robotic manipulation remains a major challenge in robotics, exemplified by piano playing, which requires coordinated control of fingers and provides a demanding testbed for reinforcement learning (RL). Although previous work established a benchmark for robotic piano playing, it is restricted to two hands and does not support unified evaluation. To address this gap, we introduce OmniPiano, a benchmark that provides one to up to five Shadow Hands and supports standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent RL within a shared piano-playing task family. OmniPiano is developed for scalable and diverse piano-playing tasks with configurable perturbations, explicit safety constraints, and decentralized cooperation settings. Particularly, to facilitate usability and extendability, OmniPiano adopts a highly modular design and provides comprehensive tasks to support RL study of task performance, robustness, safety, and cooperation in dexterous control. With at least 912 task settings and 36 baseline algorithms, OmniPiano further incorporates LLM-based agents to broaden the evaluation scope and reveal new insights. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art RL algorithms and frontier LLM-based agents still struggle on challenging piano-playing tasks, even under standard RL settings, highlighting substantial room for improvement in dexterous control. The code, dataset, tutorial, and demo are available at https://sail-research-lab.github.io/omnipiano/.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Zhicheng He, Xiaohan Xing, Hongqiu Wang, Kun Yuan, Guankun Wang
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: SurgPace introduces a complexity-aware framework for progressive distillation of surgical multimodal large language models, enhancing efficiency and stability in training through tailored supervision strategies.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Positive Safety Margins from Artificial Potential Field Reward Augmentation for Size-Robust Obstacle Avoidance under Partial Observability
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The paper demonstrates that augmenting reinforcement learning rewards with an artificial potential field can significantly enhance obstacle avoidance safety margins under partial observability, achieving high success rates.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Collision-free reaching is central to manipulation, yet real cells often leave the size and exact position of an obstacle unobserved, which excludes reinforcement learning controllers that take obstacle geometry as input. A reward limited to a collision penalty does not depend on the clearance outside the obstacle, so under a step cost its learned policy skims the obstacle surface and fails once the obstacle radius exceeds its training value. We investigate whether a single analytic reward term can induce a safety margin without exposing the obstacle to the policy. We augment the reward of a simulated Franka Emika Panda reaching task with a horizontal artificial potential field that penalizes proximity within a safety margin around each of two pillars (fixed nominal layout, random drift). Under hidden observation, policies trained with this term maintain a safe success rate above 88% across a radius sweep from 0.03 m to 0.055 m (30 seeds), while policies without it fall below 10% at the maximum tested radius; the term induces a minimum clearance of 47.9 mm against 9.6 mm without it and eliminates training collisions at least eight times earlier (median steps). The advantage is statistically significant at all out-of-distribution radii and holds across three reinforcement learning solvers and under full observation. Its safe success rate is comparable to that of a classical potential-field planner given the pillar positions. The margin is a fixed buffer rather than an adaptation to the radius, and it lengthens the path by about 19%.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: PointPilot: Unified Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric 3D Point Flow Prediction
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Yihan Fang, Yuxin Tian, Ruixiang Wang, Zhanqi Zhang, Xing Hu
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: PointPilot is a unified robotic manipulation framework that predicts 3D point flow for task-focused objects, enabling zero-shot generalization across diverse embodiments and manipulation modes.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Generalization remains a central challenge in robotics, calling for policies that address domain variations from multiple dimensions such as diverse embodiments, camera poses, and/or scene layouts. In order to approach this problem, we introduce PointPilot, a task-focused and 3D aligned manipulation framework built on a 3D space point-flow prediction. Rather than modeling the global scene, PointPilot only represents task-focused objects (robot grippers treated as objects), avoiding the prediction of potentially redundant scene parts unrelated to the manipulation tasks. Moreover, PointPilot aligns 3D spatial representation in one unified coordinate and supports closed-loop and fully automatic action execution across different manipulation modes from object point flow without a separately trained action expert, while existing works typically need an extra action head or are (semi-)automatic and single-arm mode specific. Given sensor observations and language instructions, our model jointly learns subtask planning, task-relevant object grounding, and 3D point flow prediction in an end-to-end way. By processing heterogeneous data in a shared 3D point flow space, PointPilot is able to absorb demonstrations from different embodiments. Extensive simulative and real world experiments validate our method. Notably, we demonstrate zero-shot embodiment generalization with PointPilot. A single trained policy can be deployed on previously unseen embodiments and successfully complete manipulation tasks without any additional fine-tuning.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Self-Evolving Agentic Workflows via Semantic Decomposition of Complex Tasks
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Zichuan Fu, Junjia Qi, Xian Wu, Wenlin Zhang, Yimin Deng
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The paper presents a framework for self-evolving agentic workflows that optimizes complex task execution through semantic decomposition and iterative refinement based on execution feedback.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Agentic workflows organize complex tasks into reusable procedures. However, invoking an LLM at every step incurs repeated inference costs and delays. We propose a framework for self-evolving agentic workflows through semantic task decomposition. Each subtask has explicit applicability conditions and a procedure that executes code or invokes a model as needed. An agent uses execution feedback to refine the decomposition and update these procedures. Experiments in the GLEE competition show the framework on bargaining, negotiation and persuasion. Most observed final-decision procedures are implemented in code. Code is available at https://github.com/Applied-Machine-Learning-Lab/NeurIPS2026_SeaFlow.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Efficient Agentic Audio-Visual Question Answering through Toolset Pruning and Modality Consolidation
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Peter Bell
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: This paper demonstrates that a compact omni-modal agent for audio-visual question answering can achieve similar or improved accuracy while reducing inference costs by 70% compared to specialized agents.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Fine-grained audio-visual question answering (AVQA) requires models to resolve complex cross-modal correspondences and temporally grounding from sparsely distributed evidence. Omni-modal agents, which autonomously orchestrate perception tools to actively collect evidence, achieve strong performance, but it remains unclear whether active perception from both audio and visual modalities depends on broad specialized toolsets, especially audio or visual modality-specific tools. Such systems may also introduce long execution trajectories and substantial inference cost. We investigate whether comparable performance can be retained with a compact workflow exposing only essential perceptual capabilities. Starting from the specialized-tool OmniAgent, we conduct staged controlled experiments that prune the toolset and progressively consolidate modality-specific tools into omni-modal tools, motivating a two-tool agent comprising only Omni-modal captioning and Omni-modal QA. Across three widely used AVQA benchmarks, our compact agent achieves comparable or better accuracy than the specialized-tool agent while reducing inference cost by around 70%.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: UA-Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Restoration for Material-Agnostic Object Manipulation
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Rui Cao, Jia-Hui Pan, Yin Zhang, Qiwei Meng, Jiapeng Li
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: UA-Depth is an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that enhances robotic manipulation by improving depth accuracy for non-Lambertian objects through iterative co-refinement and uncertainty-gated features.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation requires accurate metric depth, yet commodity RGB-D cameras often fail on non-Lambertian objects such as transparent, reflective, and translucent materials, producing holes, structured noise, and biased depth. We present UA-Depth, an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that iteratively co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty, and uses uncertainty-gated features to suppress unreliable cues for stable updates. To strengthen zero-shot behavior, UA-Depth leverages a frozen depth foundation model as a prior to initialize missing or unreliable depth, and applies two-stage MAD-weighted log-depth scale normalization to reduce outlier bias in relative-to-metric alignment. We introduce an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark across diverse scenes, materials, and sensors. Across these benchmarks, UA-Depth achieves the best mean rank among representative baselines, with particularly strong gains on datasets dominated by transparent and reflective objects. Beyond depth metrics, we demonstrate downstream improvements in category-level 6D pose estimation and 6D grasp synthesis by exploiting the predicted uncertainty. \emph{Code, models, and data for training and evaluation will be released upon publication.}
