On a Unitree G1, the deployed policy recovered in 95 of 150 attempts across seven real-world obstacle scenes, including furniture and multi-object arrangements absent from training. Project page: https://lu-yidan.github.io/ROOF/

OpenDriveLab.title: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Zhicheng He, Xiaohan Xing, Hongqiu Wang, Kun Yuan, Guankun Wang
OpenDriveLab.summary: SurgPace introduces a complexity-aware framework for progressive distillation of surgical multimodal large language models, enhancing efficiency and stability in training through tailored supervision strategies.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

OpenDriveLab.title: Positive Safety Margins from Artificial Potential Field Reward Augmentation for Size-Robust Obstacle Avoidance under Partial Observability
OpenDriveLab.summary: The paper demonstrates that augmenting reinforcement learning rewards with an artificial potential field can significantly enhance obstacle avoidance safety margins under partial observability, achieving high success rates.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Collision-free reaching is central to manipulation, yet real cells often leave the size and exact position of an obstacle unobserved, which excludes reinforcement learning controllers that take obstacle geometry as input. A reward limited to a collision penalty does not depend on the clearance outside the obstacle, so under a step cost its learned policy skims the obstacle surface and fails once the obstacle radius exceeds its training value. We investigate whether a single analytic reward term can induce a safety margin without exposing the obstacle to the policy. We augment the reward of a simulated Franka Emika Panda reaching task with a horizontal artificial potential field that penalizes proximity within a safety margin around each of two pillars (fixed nominal layout, random drift). Under hidden observation, policies trained with this term maintain a safe success rate above 88% across a radius sweep from 0.03 m to 0.055 m (30 seeds), while policies without it fall below 10% at the maximum tested radius; the term induces a minimum clearance of 47.9 mm against 9.6 mm without it and eliminates training collisions at least eight times earlier (median steps). The advantage is statistically significant at all out-of-distribution radii and holds across three reinforcement learning solvers and under full observation. Its safe success rate is comparable to that of a classical potential-field planner given the pillar positions. The margin is a fixed buffer rather than an adaptation to the radius, and it lengthens the path by about 19%.

OpenDriveLab.title: PointPilot: Unified Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric 3D Point Flow Prediction
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Yihan Fang, Yuxin Tian, Ruixiang Wang, Zhanqi Zhang, Xing Hu
OpenDriveLab.summary: PointPilot is a unified robotic manipulation framework that predicts 3D point flow for task-focused objects, enabling zero-shot generalization across diverse embodiments and manipulation modes.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Generalization remains a central challenge in robotics, calling for policies that address domain variations from multiple dimensions such as diverse embodiments, camera poses, and/or scene layouts. In order to approach this problem, we introduce PointPilot, a task-focused and 3D aligned manipulation framework built on a 3D space point-flow prediction. Rather than modeling the global scene, PointPilot only represents task-focused objects (robot grippers treated as objects), avoiding the prediction of potentially redundant scene parts unrelated to the manipulation tasks. Moreover, PointPilot aligns 3D spatial representation in one unified coordinate and supports closed-loop and fully automatic action execution across different manipulation modes from object point flow without a separately trained action expert, while existing works typically need an extra action head or are (semi-)automatic and single-arm mode specific. Given sensor observations and language instructions, our model jointly learns subtask planning, task-relevant object grounding, and 3D point flow prediction in an end-to-end way. By processing heterogeneous data in a shared 3D point flow space, PointPilot is able to absorb demonstrations from different embodiments. Extensive simulative and real world experiments validate our method. Notably, we demonstrate zero-shot embodiment generalization with PointPilot. A single trained policy can be deployed on previously unseen embodiments and successfully complete manipulation tasks without any additional fine-tuning.

OpenDriveLab.title: Self-Evolving Agentic Workflows via Semantic Decomposition of Complex Tasks
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Zichuan Fu, Junjia Qi, Xian Wu, Wenlin Zhang, Yimin Deng
OpenDriveLab.summary: The paper presents a framework for self-evolving agentic workflows that optimizes complex task execution through semantic decomposition and iterative refinement based on execution feedback.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Agentic workflows organize complex tasks into reusable procedures. However, invoking an LLM at every step incurs repeated inference costs and delays. We propose a framework for self-evolving agentic workflows through semantic task decomposition. Each subtask has explicit applicability conditions and a procedure that executes code or invokes a model as needed. An agent uses execution feedback to refine the decomposition and update these procedures. Experiments in the GLEE competition show the framework on bargaining, negotiation and persuasion. Most observed final-decision procedures are implemented in code. Code is available at https://github.com/Applied-Machine-Learning-Lab/NeurIPS2026_SeaFlow.

OpenDriveLab.title: Efficient Agentic Audio-Visual Question Answering through Toolset Pruning and Modality Consolidation
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Peter Bell
OpenDriveLab.summary: This paper demonstrates that a compact omni-modal agent for audio-visual question answering can achieve similar or improved accuracy while reducing inference costs by 70% compared to specialized agents.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Fine-grained audio-visual question answering (AVQA) requires models to resolve complex cross-modal correspondences and temporally grounding from sparsely distributed evidence. Omni-modal agents, which autonomously orchestrate perception tools to actively collect evidence, achieve strong performance, but it remains unclear whether active perception from both audio and visual modalities depends on broad specialized toolsets, especially audio or visual modality-specific tools. Such systems may also introduce long execution trajectories and substantial inference cost. We investigate whether comparable performance can be retained with a compact workflow exposing only essential perceptual capabilities. Starting from the specialized-tool OmniAgent, we conduct staged controlled experiments that prune the toolset and progressively consolidate modality-specific tools into omni-modal tools, motivating a two-tool agent comprising only Omni-modal captioning and Omni-modal QA. Across three widely used AVQA benchmarks, our compact agent achieves comparable or better accuracy than the specialized-tool agent while reducing inference cost by around 70%.

OpenDriveLab.title: UA-Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Restoration for Material-Agnostic Object Manipulation
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Rui Cao, Jia-Hui Pan, Yin Zhang, Qiwei Meng, Jiapeng Li
OpenDriveLab.summary: UA-Depth is an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that enhances robotic manipulation by improving depth accuracy for non-Lambertian objects through iterative co-refinement and uncertainty-gated features.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation requires accurate metric depth, yet commodity RGB-D cameras often fail on non-Lambertian objects such as transparent, reflective, and translucent materials, producing holes, structured noise, and biased depth. Most restoration methods produce only a single depth map, treating noisy and reliable regions uniformly for downstream tasks while ignoring regional uncertainty. We present UA-Depth, an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that iteratively co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty, and uses uncertainty-gated features to suppress unreliable cues for stable updates. To strengthen zero-shot behavior, UA-Depth leverages a frozen depth foundation model as a prior to initialize missing or unreliable depth, and applies two-stage MAD-weighted log-depth scale normalization to reduce outlier bias in relative-to-metric alignment. We introduce an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark across diverse scenes, materials, and sensors. Across these benchmarks, UA-Depth achieves the best mean rank among representative baselines, with particularly strong gains on datasets dominated by transparent and reflective objects. Beyond depth metrics, we demonstrate downstream improvements in category-level 6D pose estimation and 6D grasp synthesis by exploiting the predicted uncertainty. \emph{Code, models, and data for training and evaluation will be released upon publication.}

OpenDriveLab.title: GSExplorer: Interactive World Generation with a Persistent 3D Gaussian World State
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Sicheng Yu, Liu Liu, Xinjie Wang, Xinjiang Wang, Taojun Ding
OpenDriveLab.summary: GSExplorer introduces a persistent 3D Gaussian world state for interactive world generation, enhancing scene consistency and camera control through a novel generation-reconstruction framework.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Interactive world generation requires both accurate local control and stable scene consistency over long rollouts. Existing methods improve local generation through camera or geometry conditioning and extend historical context with memory mechanisms. However, long-horizon exploration remains challenging as target-view guidance becomes incomplete and inconsistencies accumulate across repeated scene updates. We present \textbf{GSExplorer}, a generation--reconstruction framework built around a persistent 3D Gaussian world state. At each step, the current 3DGS scene provides multimodal rendering conditions for a condition-driven video generator, while camera geometry is injected through a separate Relative Ray Encoding branch. Generated videos are then fed back to a SLAM-based reconstruction backend, where inconsistency filtering prevents conflicting content from corrupting the scene and cross-chunk bundle adjustment improves spatial alignment across generation steps. We further design a data-construction pipeline that reproduces realistic 3DGS degradation during scene extrapolation, yielding 293K training pairs of degraded multimodal renderings and real target videos. GSExplorer achieves the best overall performance among the compared methods on both single-step and three-step WorldScore evaluation, with strong camera control and consistency across both settings, including a Camera Control score of 99.07 in single-step extrapolation. On 481-frame leave-and-return rollouts, it also shows strong revisit consistency, demonstrating the value of maintaining a reliable 3D world state for continued exploration.

OpenDriveLab.title: ExeWorldBench: Benchmarking Code-Based Executable 3D World Modeling
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Xinge Peng, Zhen Fang, Ruibing Wang, Yongxuan Lv, Haodong Li
OpenDriveLab.summary: ExeWorldBench is a novel benchmark for evaluating code-based 3D world modeling, integrating world understanding and executable realization across three progressively challenging tasks.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Coding agents are increasingly evolving beyond reproducing what a world looks like toward constructing executable worlds that capture how a world works. This shift calls for executable world modeling, which integrates two core capabilities: world understanding, reasoning about the underlying structural, mechanical, and causal principles of a world, and executable realization, translating that understanding into a code-based system whose behavior emerges from physical interactions. However, existing benchmarks provide only fragmented evaluations centered on physical reasoning, visual fidelity, or behavioral correctness, leaving the integration of these capabilities insufficiently assessed. To bridge this gap, we introduce ExeWorldBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark to comprehensively evaluate world understanding and executable realization through code-based 3D world construction. ExeWorldBench comprises three progressively challenging tasks: Mechanism Executability, which evaluates the realization of individual mechanisms from visual observations; Compositional Executability, which extends to multi-stage systems with spatial, mechanical, and causal dependencies; and Intent-Driven Executable World Synthesis, which requires constructing executable worlds from high-level goals and physical requirements. Extensive experiments on frontier models reveal substantial limitations in executable world modeling, offering insights into the development of more physically grounded and causally coherent world construction systems.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: TailorRig: Controllable and Structured Auxiliary Skeleton Generation for Garment-Aware Rigging
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Yajing Chen, Xin Chen, Saidan Lu, Yeqi Yuan, Weikai Chen
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: TailorRig introduces a structured framework for artist-driven humanoid rigging, enhancing control over auxiliary skeleton generation and improving skinning stability for complex garments.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Humanoid rigging for modern characters with complex garments remains challenging due to the need for dense auxiliary skeletons and precise skinning control. Existing automatic methods primarily recover rigs from geometry, providing limited artist control over auxiliary articulation and often lacking explicit semantic or kinematic-chain structure for dense garment bones, leading to instability and weight bleeding. We present TailorRig, a framework that reformulates garment-aware humanoid rigging as a structured, controllable full-rig generation problem. This formulation shifts the goal from automatic rig recovery to artist-driven rig authoring, where both body-template compatibility and auxiliary articulation are explicit design choices. TailorRig exposes two explicit axes of artist control within a unified framework: a user-specified body skeleton template that preserves body-rig compatibility, and artist-provided semantic labels that drive an autoregressive generator to synthesize requested category-specific auxiliary bone chains. To robustly assign skinning weights under dense skeletal configurations, we further introduce a hierarchical chain-to-bone formulation: vertices are first associated to a kinematic chain, and bone weights are then refined within that chain, reducing weight bleeding between spatially adjacent but semantically unrelated structures. We evaluate TailorRig on a diverse set of characters and introduce Human-Mix, a large-scale dataset of over 38,000 humanoid models curated for garment-aware rigging. Experiments show that TailorRig improves skeleton accuracy, deformation stability, controllability, and practical usability over existing methods.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: DiffCap-Bench: A Comprehensive, Challenging, Robust Benchmark for Image Difference Captioning
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Yuancheng Wei, Haojie Zhang, Linli Yao, Lei Li, Jiali Chen
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: DiffCap-Bench introduces a robust benchmark for Image Difference Captioning, addressing existing evaluation gaps and enhancing multimodal language model assessments through diverse categories and human-validated metrics.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Image Difference Captioning (IDC) generates natural language descriptions that precisely identify differences between two images, serving as a key benchmark for fine-grained change perception, cross-modal reasoning, and image editing data construction. However, existing benchmarks lack diversity and compositional complexity, and standard lexical-overlap metrics (e.g., BLEU, METEOR) fail to capture semantic consistency or penalize hallucinations, which together prevent a comprehensive and robust evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on IDC. To address these gaps, we introduce DiffCap-Bench, a comprehensive IDC benchmark covering ten distinct difference categories to ensure diversity and compositional complexity. Furthermore, we propose an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation protocol grounded in human-validated Difference Lists, enabling a robust assessment of models' ability to both capture and describe visual changes. Through extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art MLLMs, we reveal significant performance gaps between proprietary and open-source models, highlight the critical importance of reasoning capability, and identify clear limitations in model scaling. Our framework also demonstrates strong alignment with human expert judgments and strong correlation with downstream image editing data construction quality. These findings establish DiffCap-Bench as both a reliable IDC evaluation framework and a practical predictor of downstream utility. The benchmark and code will be made publicly available to support further research.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Transfer the Style, Not the Semantics: Mitigating Semantic Leakage in Image-Guided Stylization
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Haojun Tang, Qiwei Lin, Tongda Xu, Wenda Zhao, Yian Zhao
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper introduces SuRe, a framework that mitigates semantic leakage in image-guided stylization by disrupting key-value correspondence in self-attention mechanisms of diffusion models.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Image-guided zero-shot style transfer enables training-free stylization of arbitrary content images using a reference style. Despite recent progress, existing methods commonly rely on self-attention manipulation to inject style information, which may transfer semantic content from the style image, leading to semantic leakage. In this work, we revisit this phenomenon from the perspective of key--value coupling in the self-attention of diffusion models. Our analysis shows that the native correspondence between style keys and values plays an important role in transferring semantic information from the style image. Motivated by this observation, we propose SuRe, a timestep-aware key--value regulation framework that mitigates semantic leakage by disrupting the native key--value correspondence while progressively restoring it for faithful style transfer. Specifically, we present value shuffle to decouple style keys and values while preserving the empirical distribution of the values, together with a progressive recoupling mechanism that gradually recouples them throughout the stylization process. Experiments against 18 representative methods demonstrate that SuRe maintains competitive style similarity while consistently improving content similarity across SD1.5, SDXL, SD3, and FLUX.1-dev, with natural generalization to multi-style transfer. The code will be publicly available at https://github.com/XinR-Tang/SuRe.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: MIRA: Reinforcing Multimodal Reasoning via Deceptive Contextual Augmentation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zhihan Yin, Jianxin Liang, Yifeng Yao, Nonghai Zhang, and Bingyue Peng
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: MIRA enhances multimodal reasoning by using deceptive visual contexts to strengthen robustness against misleading information and improve logical reasoning without human annotations.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: While Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has significantly advanced multimodal reasoning, existing frameworks suffer from a critical "perception-reasoning gap." Due to an over-reliance on seemingly relevant visual tokens, even minor perceptual perturbations can propagate through the reasoning process, leading to compounding hallucinations. To address this issue, we propose MIRA, a training framework that improves robustness to erroneous visual contexts while enhancing logical reasoning ability. By injecting filtered, deceptive visual contexts during training, we construct challenging "hard traps" that stress-test the model's robustness to misleading information. Furthermore, we introduce a group-wise reflection-triggering mechanism that enables the model to autonomously detect and rectify inconsistencies between visual cues and logical constraints, which is ultimately internalized as an intrinsic policy behavior. Importantly, MIRA does not rely on human annotations. Experimental results across multiple reasoning and perception benchmarks show that MIRA yields an average 7% improvement on in-domain benchmarks, with consistent improvements on vision-centric benchmarks. These findings highlight that active error recovery is essential for robust multimodal reasoning. Comprehensive ablation studies and analyses further provide insights into why MIRA is effective.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: ReWorld: Multi-Dimensional Reward Modeling for Embodied Video Generation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Baorui Peng, Wenyao Zhang, Liang Xu, Bohan Li, Hu Zhu
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: ReWorld introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enhances embodied video generation by aligning it with physical realism, task logic, and visual quality through a multi-dimensional reward model.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Current embodied video generation models primarily emphasize visual generative quality while overlooking physical fidelity, dynamic consistency, and task logic, especially for contact-rich manipulation tasks, which limits their applicability to downstream tasks. In this paper, we introduce ReWorld, a framework aimed to employ reinforcement learning to align the video generation with physical realism, task completion capability, embodiment plausibility and visual quality. Specifically, we first construct a large-scale (~235K) video preference dataset and employ it to train a hierarchical reward model designed to capture multi-dimensional reward consistent with human preferences. We further propose a practical alignment algorithm that post-trains flow-based video generators using this reward through a computationally efficient PPO-style algorithm. Comprehensive experiments and theoretical analysis demonstrate that ReWorld significantly improves the physical fidelity, logical coherence, embodiment and visual quality of generated rollouts, outperforming previous methods.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: LegoEnv: Self-Evolving Agentic Environments via Modular Recombination
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zhuosong Jiang, Chengxu Wu, Junqi Liu, Yujie Yi, Siqin Wang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: LegoEnv introduces a modular approach to environment design, enabling the reuse and evolution of environment components, significantly improving agent performance across diverse applications.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: LLM agents learn by interacting with environments, yet existing environments are designed for specific tasks and fail to generalize to new ones. Recent methods automate environment construction with LLMs. However, they generate each environment from scratch, neither reusing parts shared across environments nor carrying a fix from one environment to the rest. To address this, we propose a new paradigm of evolving environment atoms, which composes environments from reusable atoms (intent, rule, data and server) and evolves the atoms when an environment fails to give reliable feedback (e.g., an application lacks a tool the task requires). To instantiate this paradigm, we introduce LegoEnv, which builds 5,465 verified environments over 223 applications, and one round of evolution raises the share of solvable environments from 71.6% to 88.3%. On AutomationBench, SFT on these environments lifts Qwen3.6-27B from 16.0% to 32.0%, and RL with their verifiers lifts Qwen3.8-27B from 37.6% to 40.3%. Further analyses show steady gains with corpus size, transfer to unseen applications, and failures concentrated in a few shared root causes.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: GazeVLA: Learning Human Intention for Robotic Manipulation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Chengyang Li, Kaiyi Xiong, Yuan Xu, Lei Qian, Yizhou Wang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: GazeVLA leverages human gaze to model intentions for robotic manipulation, enhancing learning from demonstrations and improving task execution across diverse embodiments.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Embodied foundation models have significantly propelled the advancement of artificial general intelligence, yet they rely heavily on large-scale data. Recent studies identify human behavior as one of the most scalable sources for fostering robotic physical intelligence. However, the inherent embodiment gap remains a fundamental challenge for effective human-to-robot learning. In this work, we model human intention to enable efficient learning from human demonstrations. Among human behavioral cues, gaze simultaneously encodes high-level task semantics and exhibits a synergistic coupling with low-level action. By modeling intention through gaze, we derive a mid-level representation that facilitates cross-embodiment knowledge transfer. We demonstrate that robots can internalize human intentions to enhance manipulation, even without robotic intention annotations. To capture the synergy between intention and action, we adopt a Chain-of-Thought reasoning paradigm during inference. Our approach enables the execution of long-horizon and fine-grained tasks across diverse embodiments. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms baseline approaches and generalizes to unseen settings. Project page: https://gazevla.github.io .

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Text-Assisted Event Stream Visual Place Recognition via Multi-Scale Spatiotemporal Optimal Transport
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Lan Chen, Xingxing Xiong, Xiao Wang, Ziyan Zhang, Zikang Yan
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: This paper presents MSTOT-EPR, a multi-scale spatiotemporal optimal transport method that enhances visual place recognition by aligning event streams with text descriptions.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Benefiting from the high dynamic range, high temporal resolution, and low energy consumption of event cameras, low-altitude economic research leveraging event cameras has become a popular topic. Several existing attempts introduce natural-language descriptions into visual place recognition (VPR) to mitigate the sparsity of structural spatial information inherent to event cameras. Nevertheless, these methods still fail to fully address two core challenges: effectively encoding event streams and semantically aligning event streams with text. In this paper, we propose a multi-scale spatial-temporal optimal transport approach, MSTOT-EPR, to address these challenges. Specifically, given event streams and scene text information, we first adopt a visual encoder and a text encoder to extract respective feature representations. We then apply optimal-transport constraints to achieve cross-modal alignment. We then design a cross-modal bottleneck fusion module to further fuse bimodal features. Furthermore, we develop multi-scale spatial optimal transport and inter-frame temporal optimal transport modules to mine high-quality spatial-temporal event features for scene recognition. Extensive experiments on the NYC-Event-VPR and EPRBench datasets fully validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework for event-based VPR. The source code of this paper will be released upon acceptance.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Vision-Language Models Are Joint Denoisers in Robotic Action Generation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Xicheng Gong, Wenxuan Song, Chengze Liu, Qiwei Li, Qize Yu
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: JADE enhances robotic action generation by enabling joint denoising between vision-language models and action experts, improving performance and efficiency in diverse tasks.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) models cascade pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with diffusion action experts, but typically restrict the VLM to providing static conditioning. This separation limits how much pretrained perception and reasoning can guide action generation, especially in out-of-distribution settings. We introduce JADE, a Joint Action DEnoiser that enables the VLM and action expert to jointly refine actions. Our key insight is that structured action latents allow the VLM to read the current noisy action together with visual observations and language instructions. At every denoising step, the VLM contextualizes the noisy action and guides the action expert through gated cross-attention, so that its guidance evolves with the action being generated. We further supervise the VLM to recover clean action latents from noisy ones, which gives it a direct action-learning signal and couples perception with control. Additionally, joint denoising enables JADE to generate actions with fewer sampling steps, helping offset the additional cost of VLM participation. An adaptive step-size schedule further balances task performance and inference latency. On RoboDojo, JADE achieves an average success rate of 12.67%, the highest among the evaluated $π_{0.5}$-based methods, and is competitive with recent VLA and WAM foundation models pretrained at scale. It also improves performance on RoboTwin 2.0 and raises the average success rate across four real-world bimanual tasks by 20.8 percentage points compared with $π_{0.5}$.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: PS-DLO: Property- and Spatially Aware Deformable Linear Object Manipulation Policy
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Mengdi Li, Boxian Yao, Xiyu Zhu, Yunfan Lou, Yifan Yang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: PS-DLO is a manipulation policy that enhances deformable linear object handling by integrating property awareness and spatial features, achieving superior performance in various tasks.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Deformable linear objects (DLO) pose a coupled perception and control challenge: their slender geometry makes precise localization difficult, while their deformations depend on object-specific physical properties. To address this challenge, we propose PS-DLO, a property- and spatially aware DLO manipulation policy. First, contrastive image-text learning maps the initial observation to categorical descriptions of DLO properties, providing explicit physical and structural priors for action generation. Second, SAM3 extracts mask-guided features from future observations, which are distilled into the policy's action expert to encode task-relevant DLO regions and their subsequent configurations. We evaluate PS-DLO on nine real-world tasks across single-arm and bimanual platforms, training a shared multi-task policy for each embodiment. PS-DLO achieves an average success rate of 68.9%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 20.0 percentage points. In generalization experiments, PS-DLO achieves higher success rates than the baseline in six of seven visual-shift conditions on butterfly-knot untying. These results demonstrate that combining object-property priors with future spatial supervision improves multi-task DLO manipulation and robustness to visual variation.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yajing Chen, Xin Chen, Saidan Lu, Yeqi Yuan, Weikai Chen
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: TailorRig introduces a structured framework for artist-driven humanoid rigging, enhancing control over auxiliary skeleton generation and improving skinning stability for complex garments.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Embodied foundation models have significantly propelled the advancement of artificial general intelligence, yet they rely heavily on large-scale data. 智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Benefiting from the high dynamic range, high temporal resolution, and low energy consumption of event cameras, low-altitude economic research leveraging event cameras has become a popular topic. Specifically, given event streams and scene text information, we first adopt a visual encoder and a text encoder to extract respective feature representations. We then apply optimal-transport constraints to achieve cross-modal alignment. We then design a cross-modal bottleneck fusion module to further fuse bimodal features. Furthermore, we develop multi-scale spatial optimal transport and inter-frame temporal optimal transport modules to mine high-quality spatial-temporal event features for scene recognition. The source code of this paper will be released upon acceptance.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Vision-Language Models Are Joint Denoisers in Robotic Action Generation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Xicheng Gong, Wenxuan Song, Chengze Liu, Qiwei Li, Qize Yu
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: JADE enhances robotic action generation by enabling joint denoising between vision-language models and action experts, improving performance and efficiency in diverse tasks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) models cascade pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with diffusion action experts, but typically restrict the VLM to providing static conditioning. We introduce JADE, a Joint Action DEnoiser that enables the VLM and action expert to jointly refine actions. Our key insight is that structured action latents allow the VLM to read the current noisy action together with visual observations and language instructions. At every denoising step, the VLM contextualizes the noisy action and guides the action expert through gated cross-attention, so that its guidance evolves with the action being generated. We further supervise the VLM to recover clean action latents from noisy ones, which gives it a direct action-learning signal and couples perception with control. Additionally, joint denoising enables JADE to generate actions with fewer sampling steps, helping offset the additional cost of VLM participation. An adaptive step-size schedule further balances task performance and inference latency. On RoboDojo, JADE achieves an average success rate of 12.67%, the highest among the evaluated $π_{0.5}$-based methods, and is competitive with recent VLA and WAM foundation models pretrained at scale. 智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: PS-DLO: Property- and Spatially Aware Deformable Linear Object Manipulation Policy
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Mengdi Li, Boxian Yao, Xiyu Zhu, Yunfan Lou, Yifan Yang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: PS-DLO is a manipulation policy that enhances deformable linear object handling by integrating property awareness and spatial features, achieving superior performance in various tasks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Deformable linear objects (DLO) pose a coupled perception and control challenge: their slender geometry makes precise localization difficult, while their deformations depend on object-specific physical properties. To address this challenge, we propose PS-DLO, a property- and spatially aware DLO manipulation policy. First, contrastive image-text learning maps the initial observation to categorical descriptions of DLO properties, providing explicit physical and structural priors for action generation. Second, SAM3 extracts mask-guided features from future observations, which are distilled into the policy's action expert to encode task-relevant DLO regions and their subsequent configurations. PS-DLO achieves an average success rate of 68.9%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 20.0 percentage points. In generalization experiments, PS-DLO achieves higher success rates than the baseline in six of seven visual-shift conditions on butterfly-knot untying. These results demonstrate that combining object-property priors with future spatial supervision improves multi-task DLO manipulation and robustness to visual variation.

HMI Lab.title: TailorRig: Controllable and Structured Auxiliary Skeleton Generation for Garment-Aware Rigging
HMI Lab.authors_text: Yajing Chen, Xin Chen, Saidan Lu, Yeqi Yuan, Weikai Chen
HMI Lab.summary: TailorRig introduces a structured framework for artist-driven humanoid rigging, enhancing control over auxiliary skeleton generation and improving skinning stability for complex garments.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Humanoid rigging for modern characters with complex garments remains challenging due to the need for dense auxiliary skeletons and precise skinning control. Existing automatic methods primarily recover rigs from geometry, providing limited artist control over auxiliary articulation and often lacking explicit semantic or kinematic-chain structure for dense garment bones, leading to instability and weight bleeding. We present TailorRig, a framework that reformulates garment-aware humanoid rigging as a structured, controllable full-rig generation problem. This formulation shifts the goal from automatic rig recovery to artist-driven rig authoring, where both body-template compatibility and auxiliary articulation are explicit design choices. TailorRig exposes two explicit axes of artist control within a unified framework: a user-specified body skeleton template that preserves body-rig compatibility, and artist-provided semantic labels that drive an autoregressive generator to synthesize requested category-specific auxiliary bone chains. To robustly assign skinning weights under dense skeletal configurations, we further introduce a hierarchical chain-to-bone formulation: vertices are first associated to a kinematic chain, and bone weights are then refined within that chain, reducing weight bleeding between spatially adjacent but semantically unrelated structures. We evaluate TailorRig on a diverse set of characters and introduce Human-Mix, a large-scale dataset of over 38,000 humanoid models curated for garment-aware rigging. Experiments show that TailorRig improves skeleton accuracy, deformation stability, controllability, and practical usability over existing methods.
